issues.title: [BUG] apm pack strips 'category' from Claude marketplace.json output despite it being a supported Anthropic marketplace field
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm pack` drops the `category` field from the **Claude** marketplace output
(`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) even though:

1. `category` is a documented, supported *marketplace-specific* plugin-entry
   field in Anthropic's marketplace schema, and
2. APM's own `apm.yml` `marketplace.packages[]` schema already accepts and
   validates `category`.

The result: an author who wants a category-tagged Claude marketplace cannot
generate it from `apm.yml` — `apm pack` silently strips `category`, so the
committed `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` must be hand-maintained to keep the
field. `category` is currently emitted **only** for the Codex output.

Per the [Claude Code plugin-marketplace docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces#plugin-entries):

> Each plugin entry in the `plugins` array describes a plugin and where to find
> it. You can include any field from the plugin manifest schema, such as
> `description`, `version`, `author`, `commands`, and `hooks`, plus these
> marketplace-specific fields: `source`, **`category`**, `tags`, `strict`, and
> `relevance`.

> | `category` | string | Plugin category for organization |

**To Reproduce**

`apm.yml` with both outputs enabled and `category` set on the package:

```yaml
name: catdemo
version: 1.0.0
description: category propagation demo
marketplace:
  owner:
    name: demo
  outputs:
    claude: {}
    codex: {}
  claude:
    output: out/claude-marketplace.json
  codex:
    output: out/codex-marketplace.json
  packages:
    - name: a
      source: ./plugins/a          # a minimal plugin dir with .claude-plugin/plugin.json
      version: 1.0.0
      description: demo package
      category: retrieval
```

```bash
apm pack
grep -i category out/claude-marketplace.json   # -> no match (stripped)
grep -i category out/codex-marketplace.json    # -> "category": "retrieval"
```

**Expected behavior**

`category` should be carried into each plugin entry of the **Claude** output
when present on the package, matching the Anthropic marketplace schema — just as
`tags`, `author`, `license`, `repository`, and `homepage` already are. It should
remain optional (omitted when unset).

**Environment**

- OS: macOS (Darwin)
- Python Version: 3.12
- APM Version: 0.24.1 (also confirmed on `main` @ `5875577d`)

**Logs / evidence (source)**

- `src/apm_cli/marketplace/output_mappers.py` — `ClaudeMarketplaceMapper` emits
  `name`, `description`, `version`, `author`, `license`, `repository`, `tags`,
  `homepage`, and `source`, but never `category`. `CodexMarketplaceMapper` emits
  `plugin["category"] = entry.category` (and requires it).
- `src/apm_cli/marketplace/yml_schema.py` accepts `category` as a valid
  `packages[]` field and carries the comment:
  *"Optional marketplace category. Claude output strips this; Codex output …"* —
  i.e. the strip is intentional today, but it diverges from the Anthropic schema
  that the Claude output otherwise targets byte-for-byte.

**Additional context**

Propagating `category` to the Claude output would let single-source-of-truth
producers (`apm.yml` -> `apm pack` -> `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) keep
category-tagged Claude marketplaces instead of hand-editing the generated file.
Happy to open a PR that adds the mapping + tests (the Claude mapper already has
the conditional-field pattern to follow).

issues.title: [BUG] claude_skill subpath dep records inconsistent name/version across resolution paths (install --frozen vs update), churning the lockfile
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

For a `claude_skill` virtual subpath dependency (one that has a `SKILL.md` but no `apm.yml`; e.g. `mattpocock/skills/skills/productivity/grilling`), the `name` / `version` apm records in the lockfile **changes depending on the resolution path**.

- Full resolution that regenerates the lockfile (`apm update`, and `apm install` with a warm module cache) → `name: grilling` (the skill's own name) / `version: 1.0.0`.
- `apm install --frozen` when a lockfile already exists (the path that uses the lock's cached commit and skips re-resolution) → `name: skills` (the repo name) / `version: unknown`.

Because the two disagree, alternating these two paths rewrites the lockfile every time (churn). Moreover, the `--frozen` side rewrites it silently while reporting "No changes -- install state already up to date".

Note that neither path is fully accurate on a per-field basis. For `name`, the full-resolution value `grilling` (the actual value in the `SKILL.md` frontmatter) is correct, and the cached-side `skills` (the repo name) is wrong. Conversely, for `version`, the cached-side `unknown` is truer to reality, and the full-resolution `1.0.0` is a fabricated value (this skill's `SKILL.md` frontmatter has no `version`, and the upstream repository has neither an `apm.yml` nor a tag pin, so no definite version exists anywhere; `1.0.0` is merely a hardcoded value in `_validate_claude_skill`).

## To Reproduce

1. Declare a `claude_skill` virtual subpath dependency in `apm.yml`.
   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - mattpocock/skills/skills/productivity/grilling
   ```
2. Remove the lockfile and regenerate it with `apm update`.
   ```
   rm -f apm.lock.yaml
   apm update --yes
   ```
   → The entry is `name: grilling` / `version: 1.0.0`.
3. In the same state, run `apm install --frozen` (it reports `(cached)` / `(files unchanged)` and "No changes -- install state already up to date").
   → The entry is rewritten to `name: skills` / `version: unknown`.
4. Alternating steps 2 and 3 rewrites the lockfile each time.

## Expected behavior

- For the same dependency at the same commit, `name` / `version` should be identical regardless of the resolution path (install / update / `--frozen`).
- The value to converge on should be, per field, whichever is truer to reality. In this example that is **`name: grilling` / `version: unknown`**. Rationale:
  - In the lockfile, `name` / `version` are not used as the dependency's identity key (`get_unique_key` is built from `repo_url` + `virtual_path` etc. and does not include `name` / `version`: [`deps/lockfile.py#L219-L231`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/deps/lockfile.py#L219-L231)). Since identity resolution is not broken by either value, the only question is which is the more accurate description.
  - `name`: `skills` is the repo name, not the package name. The `SKILL.md` frontmatter actually contains `name: grilling`, and apm itself deploys this skill as `grilling` (lockfile deployment: `value: .claude/skills/grilling`). The full-resolution side already reads the frontmatter and obtains `grilling` (`validation.py:458-475`). The cached side simply doesn't read it and falls back to the repo name, so `grilling` is correct.
  - `version`: this skill's `SKILL.md` frontmatter has no `version`, and the upstream repository has neither an `apm.yml` nor a tag pin. No definite version exists anywhere, so `unknown` is truer to reality. The full-resolution `1.0.0` is a hardcode in `_validate_claude_skill` ([`validation.py#L470`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/models/validation.py#L470)) with no basis in the actual data.
- Concrete fix (for each path, correct the side that is not truthful):
  - In the cached path [`CachedDependencySource.acquire()` — `install/sources.py#L481-L494`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/install/sources.py#L481-L494), in the "`apm.yml` absent" fallback, take `name` from the frontmatter before falling back to the repo name when a `SKILL.md` exists (`skills` → `grilling`).
  - In the full-resolution path `_validate_claude_skill` ([`models/validation.py#L463-L470`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/models/validation.py#L463-L470)), stop hardcoding `version="1.0.0"` and treat the version as missing when the frontmatter has no `version` (`1.0.0` → `unknown`).
  - If both paths derive `name` / `version` from the `SKILL.md` frontmatter as the single source of truth, they converge on `grilling` / `unknown` and the churn is resolved. The representation of a missing version (an `unknown` string / omitting the field / etc.) is left to apm's conventions.
- A no-op / `--frozen` install should not rewrite the lockfile. Design intent of `is_semantically_equivalent`: [`deps/lockfile.py#L953-L969`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/deps/lockfile.py#L953-L969) — *"a no-change install does not dirty the lockfile"*.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 27.0 (build 26A5378j)
- Python Version: Homebrew-distributed prebuilt binary (interpreter not visible to the user)
- APM Version: 0.25.0 (d73e6ac)
- VSCode Version: N/A

## Logs

Diff of the entry across `apm update` (lock regeneration) → `apm install --frozen`. `--frozen` reports "No changes".

```diff
  # mattpocock/skills/skills/productivity/grilling
- name: grilling
+ name: skills

- version: 1.0.0
+ version: unknown
```

```
  [+] github.com/mattpocock/skills/skills/productivity/grilling @66898f60 (cached)
  |-- (files unchanged)
[i] No changes -- install state already up to date in 0.0s.
```

## Additional context

### Confirmed source of the degraded side

The `--frozen` path (and the cached path when a lockfile already exists) goes through [`CachedDependencySource.acquire()` — `install/sources.py#L481-L494`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/install/sources.py#L481-L494). When there is no `apm.yml` directly under `install_path` (which is the case for a `claude_skill` subpath dependency), it enters this fallback:

```python
else:
    cached_package = APMPackage(
        name=dep_ref.repo_url.split("/")[-1],   # -> "skills" (repo name)
        version="unknown",
        ...
    )
```

This `name` / `version` flows into `InstalledPackage` ([`sources.py#L568-L573`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/install/sources.py#L568-L573)) → `LockedDependency` ([`deps/lockfile.py#L535-L585`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/deps/lockfile.py#L535-L585)), matching the observed `skills` / `unknown`.

### The full-resolution side, on the other hand

The full-resolution side records `name: grilling` / `version: 1.0.0` for the same dependency (confirmed in reproduction step 2). On this path, the post-download validation [`validate_apm_package` → `_validate_claude_skill` — `models/validation.py#L458-L475`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/models/validation.py#L458-L475) determines `name` / `version` from the `SKILL.md` frontmatter:

```python
skill_name = post.metadata.get("name", package_path.name)
...
package = APMPackage(
    name=skill_name,      # SKILL.md frontmatter name -> "grilling"
    version="1.0.0",      # hardcoded; the frontmatter version is not consulted
    ...
)
```

This value flows through `InstalledPackage` ([`sources.py#L813-L818`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/install/sources.py#L813-L818)) into the same `LockedDependency`.

In other words, for the identical condition "has `SKILL.md`, no `apm.yml`", the cached path (`sources.py:481-494`, repo-name fallback) and the full-resolution path (`validation.py:458-475`, frontmatter-derived) generate different `name` / `version`, and this is the cause of the churn.

### Why a write happens

The semantic-equivalence check for `LockedDependency` is done via `to_dict()` (which includes `name` / `version`) ([`deps/lockfile.py#L953-L969`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.25.0/src/apm_cli/deps/lockfile.py#L953-L969)). Therefore the discrepancy above is judged non-equivalent and a write occurs. That this write is not suppressed even under `--frozen` is being confirmed separately in discussion #2194.

### Related

- Existing (all closed) issues in the "lockfile rewritten on every run" lineage: #450, #1532, #1702, #2078. Those were idempotency false positives with unchanged content in the same scope; this issue has a different cause (the `name` / `version` themselves change by path).

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report
issues.body:
# CLI Consistency Report

**Date:** 2026-07-15  
**APM Version:** 0.25.0 (defafe3)  
**Commands Inspected:** 56 (all top-level commands plus all documented subcommands)

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|------:|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 3 |

---

# Medium Severity

## apm pack: Multi-line examples section garbled in help output

**Command:** `apm pack`

**Problem:**  
The `Examples:` and `Exit codes:` sections in `_PACK_HELP` are reflowed by Click into single run-on lines, making them difficult to read. Click merges adjacent lines within a paragraph unless they are preceded by `\b` (form-feed). The source (`pack.py`, lines 36–59) contains correct multi-line formatting, but the rendered help output collapses it.

**Evidence (rendered terminal output with `COLUMNS=200`):**

```text
Examples:

  # Bundle only (most common -- just dependencies: in apm.yml):   apm pack
  # Claude Code plugin (default)   apm pack --target claude --archive   apm
  pack --format apm -o ./dist       # Legacy APM bundle layout

  # Marketplace only (marketplace: in apm.yml, no dependencies:):   apm pack
  apm pack --offline --dry-run

Exit codes:   0  Success   1  Build or runtime error   2  Manifest schema
validation error   3  Version alignment check failed (--check-versions)   4
Marketplace working-tree drift detected (--check-clean)
```

**Suggested Fix:**  
Prefix each block that should preserve formatting with `\b\n` (Click's no-reformat sentinel). For example:

```text
Examples:
\b
  # Bundle only (most common -- just dependencies: in apm.yml):
  apm pack
```

Apply the same approach to the `Exit codes:` section and the `Reads apm.yml to decide what to produce:` bullet list.

---

## apm publish: Multi-line examples garbled and RST backticks visible in terminal

**Command:** `apm publish`

**Problem:**  
The `Examples:` section in `_PUBLISH_HELP` (`publish.py`, lines 34–47) suffers from the same Click paragraph reflow issue as `apm pack`, collapsing into run-on lines.

Additionally, the description uses reStructuredText double backticks (``apm.yml``, ``.apm/``), which are rendered literally in terminal output instead of appearing as code formatting.

**Evidence:**

```text
Reads apm.yml for the package name/version, packs a flat registry zip
archive (``apm.yml`` + ``.apm/`` at the archive root -- not ``apm pack``
plugin bundles), or uses a pre-built zip via --zip, then uploads to the
registry via PUT /v1/packages/{owner}/{repo}/versions/{version}.

Requires the 'registries' experimental feature:   apm experimental enable
registries

Examples:

  # Auto-pack and publish to the only configured registry:   apm publish
  --package acme/my-skill
```

**Suggested Fix:**

1. Replace RST double backticks with single backticks or plain text, since Click does not render RST.
2. Protect the `Examples:` section with `\b\n`, as in `apm pack`.

---

## apm cache clean: `-f/--force` and `-y/--yes` both described as "Skip confirmation prompt"

**Command:** `apm cache clean`

**Problem:**  
The command exposes two flags that perform the same action (`-f/--force` and `-y/--yes`) with identical help text.

Elsewhere in the APM CLI, `--force` consistently means "overwrite locally-authored files on collision" (e.g. `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `pack`). Using it to skip a confirmation prompt in `cache clean` is semantically inconsistent.

**Evidence (`apm cache clean --help`):**

```text
Options:
  -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
  -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
  --help       Show this message and exit.
```

Compare with `apm deps clean --help`:

```text
Options:
  --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
  -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt
  --help     Show this message and exit.
```

**Suggested Fix:**  
Remove `-f/--force` from `apm cache clean` and keep only `-y/--yes` for consistency with `apm deps clean` and the rest of the CLI.

If backward compatibility requires retaining `--force`, update its help text to:

> Alias for `--yes`; skip confirmation prompt.

---

# Low Severity

## apm targets usage line advertises `[COMMAND] [ARGS]...` but has no subcommands

**Command:** `apm targets`

**Problem:**  
The usage line displays:

```text
Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] [COMMAND] [ARGS]...
```

This implies that subcommands exist, but none are listed or implemented. Although `targets.py` intentionally uses a `click.group` for future expansion, the placeholder creates unnecessary confusion.

**Evidence:**

```text
Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] [COMMAND] [ARGS]...

Show resolved targets for the current project.

Options:
  --json
  --all
  --help
```

No `Commands:` section follows.

**Suggested Fix:**

Either:

- add `invoke_without_command=True` and mention that subcommands are planned, or
- suppress the `[COMMAND] [ARGS]...` placeholder until subcommands exist.

A simple short-term solution is to add a note such as:

> No subcommands yet; run `apm targets` to print the table.

---

## apm deps update and apm unpack use inconsistent deprecation styles

**Commands:** `apm deps update`, `apm unpack`

**Problem:**  
The two deprecated commands use different visual styles.

`apm deps update`:

```text
DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset).
```

`apm unpack`:

```text
[Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.
```

Using different formats makes deprecated commands less consistent and harder to scan.

**Suggested Fix:**  
Adopt a single style throughout the CLI.

The `[Deprecated]` prefix used by `apm unpack` is clearer and aligns better with common CLI conventions.

---

## apm run description adds "(experimental)" in the command listing

**Command:** `apm run`

**Observation:**  
Initially this appeared inconsistent, but both `apm --help` and `apm run --help` label the command as "(experimental)". The same applies to `apm runtime`.

**Evidence:**  
The top-level command listing and the command help both include the same experimental label.

**Suggested Fix:**  
No change required. The current behavior is consistent.

---

# Clean Areas

- All 33 top-level commands exist in the CLI and have corresponding documentation pages under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. No undocumented commands or missing documentation were found.
- `--help` / `-h` works correctly for every command and subcommand tested (56 total), with no crashes or stack traces.
- `--verbose` / `-v` is present and consistently implemented across all applicable commands.
- `--dry-run` is consistently named and available across supported commands (`install`, `compile`, `update`, `uninstall`, `deps clean`, `audit`, `pack`, `prune`, `unpack`, `publish`).
- `--yes` / `-y` is consistently used in `deps clean`, `runtime remove`, `update`, and `cache clean`.
- Error handling is clean. Invalid invocations such as `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (without an argument), and `apm config set` (without arguments) produce usage errors without stack traces.
- All documented `apm deps` subcommands (`list`, `tree`, `info`, `clean`, `update`, `why`) are present.
- All documented `apm mcp` subcommands (`list`, `search`, `show`, `install`) are present.
- All documented `apm config` subcommands (`get`, `set`, `list`, `unset`) are present.
- All documented `apm runtime` subcommands (`list`, `setup`, `remove`, `status`) are present.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-07-16
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-16
**APM Version**: 0.25.0 (49bfdc6)
**Commands Inspected**: 31

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 2     |
| Low      | 2     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps update --help` has stale/incomplete target list

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The `--target` option lists a significantly shorter and outdated set of values compared to the current `apm install` and `apm update` commands. Missing targets include `vscode`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `agents`, `agy`, `copilot-app`, and `copilot-cowork`. The `all` expansion description is also stale — it says "all = copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf+kiro" omitting targets added later.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm deps update --help:
    -t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                         copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                         gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-
                         skills, all. ... 'all' = co
                         pilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+wind
                         surf+kiro ...

  # apm update --help (current):
    -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                         skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                         codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                         cursor, gemini, hermes, intellij, kiro,
                         openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `apm deps update` help text to reflect the current target registry, or (since the command is deprecated) explicitly point users to `apm update` and note the expanded target set is available there. Ideally, share the target enum/list from a single source of truth so both commands always stay in sync.

---

#### `apm mcp install` forwarded flags are invisible in `--help`

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: The `--help` output buries `--dry-run`, `--verbose`, `--dev`, `--force`, and `--no-policy` in the description text as "Forwarded install options" rather than exposing them as formal Click `Options:`. Users cannot discover them via shell tab-completion, and the help section that lists them is easy to miss. This is inconsistent with how `apm install --help` exposes the same flags as full option entries with descriptions and defaults.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm mcp install --help:
  Usage: apm mcp install [OPTIONS] NAME
    ...
    Forwarded install options (see 'apm install --help' for the full list):
      --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]
      --url URL           Server URL for remote transports
      ...
      --dev / --dry-run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Only `--help` appears under `Options:`. All others are in the description paragraph.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) expose the commonly-used forwarded flags (`--dry-run`, `--verbose`, `--target`, `--dev`) as explicit Click options on the `mcp install` command so they appear in the `Options:` section and are tab-completable, or (b) add a note to the description that these flags are passed through verbatim after the NAME argument (e.g., `apm mcp install NAME [INSTALL_OPTIONS] [-- COMMAND]`).

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm init --target` is missing the `-t` short form

- **Command**: `apm init`
- **Problem**: Every other command that accepts `--target` consistently provides `-t` as the short form (`apm install -t`, `apm update -t`, `apm compile -t`, `apm lock -t`, `apm deps update -t`). `apm init` is the only exception.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm init --help:
    --target TARGET  Comma-separated target list (skip prompt, write directly)

  # apm install --help:
    -t, --target TARGET  Target harness(es) to deploy to. ...

  # apm update --help:
    -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for. ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-t` as the short form for `--target` in `apm init` to match every other command.

---

#### `apm config get` with no argument acts like `apm config list` but this is undocumented

- **Command**: `apm config get`
- **Problem**: Running `apm config get` with no `KEY` argument silently returns all configuration values (the same output as `apm config list`). The help says `[KEY]` is optional but gives no indication of what happens when it is omitted.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm config get --help:
  Usage: apm config get [OPTIONS] [KEY]
    Get a configuration value
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

  # apm config get (no argument):
  [i] APM Configuration:
    auto-integrate: true
    temp-dir: Not set (using system default)
    mcp-registry-url: Not set (using default https://api.mcp.github.com)
  ```
  No mention that omitting `KEY` lists all values.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the help description to read something like: `Get a configuration value. Omit KEY to list all values (alias for 'apm config list').`

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands/areas passed all checks:

- **Error handling**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (no arg), `apm config set` (missing args) — all produce clear error messages with usage hints; no tracebacks observed.
- **`apm install --help`**: Comprehensive, well-structured, all flags properly documented with defaults and descriptions.

issues.title: apm lock deletes dropped deployed files (pre-existing lock-mode disk deletion via _attach_deployed_files)
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm lock` (lockfile-only mode) can delete deployed instruction files from disk when a manifest target is dropped, via the pre-existing `_attach_deployed_files` path introduced in #2283. Lock mode is documented as `--package-lock-only` (it should reconcile the lockfile, not mutate the working tree), so performing filesystem deletion there is a design gap.

## Provenance / scope

- Discovered while shepherding #2295 (target-instruction contraction cleanup).
- This behavior exists at **base** (`702876b0`), independent of #2295. It is **not** introduced by #2295.
- #2295 folded a guard (`if not self.ctx.lockfile_only:`) around its *new* final-path `_reconcile_target_deployed_files` call, so after #2295 the PR is **behavior-neutral on `apm lock` versus base** -- it neither introduces nor worsens this bug. The pre-existing deletion via `_attach_deployed_files` remains.

## Why this was deferred (not folded into #2295)

Fixing it requires decoupling lockfile-row reconciliation from disk deletion inside the reconciliation path. That touches the reserved three-gate cleanup chokepoint design (`remove_stale_deployed_files`) and the ownership boundary between lockfile-row bookkeeping and filesystem mutation. It needs its own brief and its own regression + mutation-break coverage, rather than being smuggled into a contraction-cleanup PR.

## Suggested direction

- Audit `_attach_deployed_files` (approx `src/apm_cli/install/phases/lockfile.py:196-300`) and confirm which call sites can trigger disk deletion under `lockfile_only`.
- Decide the contract: `apm lock` should update the lockfile's `deployed_files` rows/hashes without unlinking on-disk files, deferring physical prune to the next `apm install`.
- Add a regression trap: `apm lock` after a target drop must leave the dropped file on disk (positive control: `apm install` still prunes it), plus a mutation-break proving the guard is load-bearing.
- Preserve all existing safety invariants: deletion (when it does happen, in install) must continue routing exclusively through the three-gate cleanup chokepoint; never add ad-hoc `unlink`/`rmtree`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `apm lock` does not delete deployed files from disk when a target is dropped.
- [ ] `apm install` still prunes dropped deployed files (behavior unchanged).
- [ ] User-edited bytes remain protected by the provenance hash gate on both paths.
- [ ] New regression test + mutation-break evidence for the lock-mode no-delete contract.
- [ ] No new deletion path outside `remove_stale_deployed_files`.

## References

- PR #2295 (target-instruction contraction cleanup; where this was discovered and deferred)
- PR #2283 (introduced `_attach_deployed_files`)

issues.title: [BUG] `.cursor/hooks.json` emits Claude-formatted hooks (`Stop`/`PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`) when installing target-scoped `*-hooks-claude` packages alongside `*-hooks-cursor` in a multi-target project
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install --update` on a project with `targets: [claude, cursor]` and separate target-scoped hook packages (`common-hooks-claude` with `target: claude`, `common-hooks-cursor` with `target: cursor`) writes Claude-formatted hook entries into `.cursor/hooks.json`:

1. PascalCase event keys (`Stop`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`) alongside correct Cursor camelCase keys (`stop`, `preToolUse`, `postToolUse`, `afterFileEdit`)
2. Claude nested schema (`{ "matcher": "", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", ... }] }`) instead of Cursor flat schema (`{ "command": "...", "timeoutSec": N }`)
3. Commands pointing at `.cursor/hooks/common-hooks-claude/scripts/...` — scripts from packages declared `target: claude`

Net effect: the PascalCase blocks are dead config in Cursor (event keys are case-sensitive; `Stop` does not match `stop`). Correct Cursor entries still work, but `.cursor/hooks.json` is polluted with unreachable Claude-format hooks. This is the reverse-direction regression of #1007 (Cursor format leaking into Claude settings).

The sidecar `.cursor/apm-hooks.json` contains only `*-hooks-cursor` sources — APM does not claim the Claude entries — yet they are written into `.cursor/hooks.json`.

**To Reproduce**

1. Clone a multi-target config repo (or create minimal repro below)
2. Ensure `apm.yml` has:
   ```yaml
   targets:
     - claude
     - cursor
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - ./.apm/packages/common-hooks-claude   # apm.yml: target: claude
       - ./.apm/packages/common-hooks-cursor   # apm.yml: target: cursor
   ```
3. Ensure `.cursor/` and `.claude/` marker dirs exist
4. Run: `apm install --update`
5. Inspect: `cat .cursor/hooks.json`
6. Compare sidecar: `cat .cursor/apm-hooks.json`

**Expected behavior**

Per [Hooks and Commands](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/producer/author-primitives/hooks-and-commands/):

> Merged hook files contain only each target's native upstream fields.

- `.cursor/hooks.json` should contain **only** Cursor-native keys (`stop`, `preToolUse`, `postToolUse`, `afterFileEdit`) in flat schema with `timeoutSec`
- Packages with `target: claude` should integrate hooks into `.claude/settings.json` (or `.claude/apm-hooks.json` sidecar), **not** into `.cursor/hooks.json`
- Claude PascalCase keys (`Stop`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`) must not appear in `.cursor/hooks.json`
- `.cursor/apm-hooks.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json` should agree on which entries APM owns

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux (linuxkit / devcontainer)
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.26.0 (64a7fb5)
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A (CLI `apm install` behavior; issue is in generated config)

**Logs**

Excerpt from `.cursor/hooks.json` after `apm install --update` (Claude-format block appended):

```json
"Stop": [
  {
    "matcher": "",
    "hooks": [
      {
        "type": "command",
        "command": ".cursor/hooks/common-hooks-claude/scripts/actionlint.sh",
        "timeout": 60
      }
    ]
  }
],
"PostToolUse": [ "..." ],
"PreToolUse": [ "..." ]
```

Correct Cursor block in the same file (works):

```json
"stop": [
  {
    "command": ".cursor/hooks/common-hooks-cursor/scripts/actionlint.sh",
    "timeoutSec": 60
  }
]
```

`.cursor/apm-hooks.json` lists only `_apm_source: common-hooks-cursor` (and `go-hooks-cursor`, `shell-script-hooks-cursor`) — no `common-hooks-claude` entries.

**Additional context**

### Related issues

- #1007 — Cursor format leaking into `.claude/settings.json` (closed in 0.9.4; same `hook_integrator.py` class)
- #1499 — user-scope hook integration (different scope)

### Hypothesis

When multiple install targets are active, `hook_integrator.py` integrates hook packages into all merged-hook targets without filtering by the dependency package's `target:` field, and/or emits source-format entries without transforming event keys for the destination target.

### Consumer repo

- `github.com/y-miyazaki/config` — intentionally ships `*-hooks-claude` and `*-hooks-cursor` as separate packages per [specification](https://github.com/y-miyazaki/config/blob/main/docs/reference/specification.md#hooks)

### Impact

Non-fatal (correct Cursor hooks still fire), but violates documented merge contract and creates dead config that confuses users and downstream validation.

issues.title: Allow SkillSpector --baseline through apm audit external args
issues.body:
### Problem

`apm audit` supports scanner-specific `--external-args`, but the SkillSpector adapter in APM 0.26.0 does not allowlist SkillSpector’s `--baseline` option. As a result, repositories cannot use SkillSpector’s reviewed baseline suppression while retaining `apm audit` as the single audit and SARIF entry point.

The desired invocation is:

```sh
apm audit --external skillspector --no-external-llm \
  --external-args "--baseline .skillspector-baseline.yaml" \
  --format sarif --output reports/skillspector.sarif
```

APM audit reference: https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/audit/

SkillSpector suppression reference: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector/blob/main/docs/SUPPRESSION.md

### Requested behavior

- Allow the long-form `--baseline` option for the SkillSpector adapter.
- Require exactly one path value.
- Resolve and validate that path using APM’s existing external-argument safety checks.
- Reject paths outside the audit working directory.
- Continue rejecting arbitrary SkillSpector arguments fail-closed.

### Suggested tests

- Accept an existing baseline path inside the working directory.
- Reject a missing value.
- Reject an absolute or relative path that escapes the working directory.
- Preserve the current behavior when no baseline is supplied.
- Confirm SARIF output excludes findings suppressed by the supplied baseline.

This would let consumers adopt exact-fingerprint SkillSpector baselines without bypassing APM or patching installed packages.

issues.title: [BUG]  A dependency's devDependencies mcp servers are installed into the consuming project
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a project depends on a git-sourced APM package, `apm install` deploys that dependency's **`devDependencies.mcp`** servers into the consuming project's MCP config (e.g. `.mcp.json` for Claude), alongside its prod `dependencies.mcp`. Dev/prod separation is honored for the dependency's APM sub-dependencies (skills from `devDependencies.apm` are correctly NOT installed), but not for its MCP servers.

Possibly a regression from the fix for #1780 (which made `apm install` honor `devDependencies.mcp` in the *authoring* project — correct there, but the same all-deps collection now applies to dependency packages too).

**To Reproduce**

1. Author package `owner/dep` whose `apm.yml` declares:
   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     mcp:
       - name: prod-server
         registry: false
         transport: http
         url: https://example.com/prod
   devDependencies:
     mcp:
       - name: dev-server
         registry: false
         transport: http
         url: https://example.com/dev
   ```
2. In a consuming project, add `owner/dep` to `dependencies.apm` and run `apm install --target claude`.
3. Inspect the consumer's `.mcp.json`: both `prod-server` **and** `dev-server` are configured. `apm.lock.yaml`'s `mcp_config_provenance` attributes both to the dependency.

**Expected behavior**

Only the dependency's prod `dependencies.mcp` servers are deployed into the consumer — matching the documented contract that devDependencies are for the package author's own development, and matching how `devDependencies.apm` of dependencies is already handled.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux (WSL2)
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.26.0 (64a7fb5)

issues.title: [BUG] Global install prunes removed files but leaves stale deployed-file hashes in the lockfile
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

On APM 0.26.0, upgrading an already installed global package to a newer exact
ref correctly removed two files that no longer exist in the package, but the
package's lock entry retained both paths in `deployed_files` and
`deployed_file_hashes`.

The physical deployment therefore matched the new package while the lockfile
still described a superset of the deployment. The package is private, so its
owner, refs, and file names are intentionally sanitized below.

**To Reproduce**

1. Prepare exact package ref `ref-a` with two deployed skill-bundle files.
2. Install it globally for the Codex target.
3. Prepare exact ref `ref-b` of the same package, removing only those two files
   while retaining the rest of the package.
4. Run:

   ```text
   apm install owner/private-package#ref-b --global --target codex --verbose
   ```

   No `--force`, `--update`, or `--refresh` flag is used.
5. Compare the package's lock entry with the deployed tree.

In the observed upgrade:

- the deployed tree correctly contained 87 files;
- `deployed_file_hashes` contained 89 entries;
- `deployed_files` contained 98 entries instead of the expected 96 (87 files
  plus nine top-level skill directory anchors); and
- the two extra paths were exactly the files removed in `ref-b`.

As a control, moving the old global package/lock state aside and installing
`ref-b` into a fresh global APM state produced the correct 87 hashes and 96
deployment entries, with the two removed paths absent. That makes this appear
specific to upgrade reconciliation from the prior lock.

**Expected behavior**

After the exact-ref install completes, the physical deployment and the
lockfile's derived deployment views should converge:

- removed files are absent from disk;
- removed paths are absent from both `deployed_files` and
  `deployed_file_hashes`; and
- every recorded file hash corresponds to an actually deployed file.

**Actual behavior**

Disk cleanup succeeds, but the prior lock's removed paths and hashes survive in
the newly generated lockfile. The command exits successfully even though the
lock asserts that two absent files remain part of the deployment.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84)
- Python Version: 3.14.6
- APM Version: 0.26.0 (`64a7fb5`)
- Target: global Codex installation
- Codex CLI: 0.146.0-alpha.3.1

**Logs**

No raw log is attached because the source package is private. The sanitized
counts and command above are from the preserved failed-verification state.

**Additional context**

This looks like a regression or sibling of
[#1831](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/1831), fixed by
[#1856](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/pull/1856): that report covered stale
files remaining on disk, whereas here disk cleanup succeeds and only the lock
retains stale paths. [#2139](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/2139) also
records the intended contract that `apm install` reconciles artifacts and lock
entries.

I searched current open and closed issues for this specific
disk-clean/lock-stale combination and did not find an exact duplicate.

issues.title: Project-scope hook path rewriting produces cwd-dependent commands on Windows (Claude Code target)
issues.body:
## Summary

For project-scope `apm install` (no `-g`), hook `command` strings that use
`${PLUGIN_ROOT}` / `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` are rewritten to a bare
repo-relative path (per `_rewrite_command_for_target` /
`_deploy_root_for_hook_rewrite` in `src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py`).
On Windows, with the Claude Code target, this produces a `command` that
fails whenever Claude Code spawns the hook process with a working directory
other than the project root.

## Reproduction

1. Install any package whose `.apm/hooks/*.json` uses `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` in a
   `PreToolUse` hook `command`, project-scope, target `claude`.
2. The merged `.claude/settings.json` ends up with e.g.:
   ```json
   "command": "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \".claude/hooks/<pkg>/.apm/hooks/scripts/<script>.ps1\""
3. Trigger the hook (an Edit/Write tool call) while Claude Code's
working directory for the hook process is not the project root.

Observed:
PreToolUse:Edit hook error
Failed with non-blocking status code: The argument '.claude/hooks/<pkg>/.apm/hooks/scripts/<script>.ps1'
to the -File parameter does not exist. Provide the path to an existing '.ps1' file
as an argument to the -File parameter.

powershell.exe -File <relative-path> resolves the file against the process's
current directory before the script itself ever runs, so the script's own
try/catch (if any) never gets a chance to fail open — the failure happens at
the launcher level.

## Root cause

@staticmethod
def _deploy_root_for_hook_rewrite(project_root: Path, user_scope: bool) -> Path | None:
    # User scope needs cwd-independent paths; project scope stays portable.
    return project_root if user_scope else None

and, in _rewrite_command_for_target:

▎ For project-scope (deploy_root is None) leave the variable in place --
▎ rewriting to an absolute path would re-introduce the #1394 portability
▎ regression in committed configs.

This correctly avoids baking a machine-specific absolute path into a
committed settings.json (which would break on every other clone/CI
runner — the #1394 regression). But it conflates "absolute path" with
"cwd-independent path" — there is a third option that is both portable
and cwd-independent: anchoring the path to Claude Code's own
$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR environment variable, which Claude Code sets for
every hook invocation specifically so hook commands don't have to assume
a particular working directory.

$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/<pkg>/... is:
- identical on every clone/CI runner (it's an env var reference, not a
baked-in path) — satisfies the same portability goal as the current
bare-relative output, and
- independent of the hook process's actual working directory — which the
current bare-relative output is not, as reproduced above.

## Proposed fix

For the claude target specifically (this env var is Claude Code's own
convention; it doesn't apply to other targets emitting from the same
source hook JSON), have project-scope rewriting emit:

$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/<rel_path>

instead of the current bare <rel_path>, when deploy_root is None and
target == "claude". This keeps _deploy_root_for_hook_rewrite's existing
contract for every other target untouched.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Shell: PowerShell (hook scripts are .ps1, invoked via
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "...")
- Install scope: project (no -g)
- Target: claude

issues.title: [BUG] apm marketplace audit skips local plugin sources instead of auditing local apm.yml files
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`apm marketplace audit NAME --strict --verbose` skips plugins whose marketplace manifest uses local source entries like `./plugins/plugin-a` or `./plugins/plugin-b`.

In a monorepo or local marketplace-authoring repo, this means the audit does not inspect any plugin `dependencies.apm` at all, even though the local plugin `apm.yml` files are present in the working tree.

In my case, the marketplace contains 2 plugins and every one of them is skipped as `unsupported_source`. The command still exits successfully in `--strict` mode.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Use a registered marketplace whose manifest packages point at local plugin sources, for example:

    ```yaml
    marketplace:
       packages:
          - name: plugin-a
             source: ./plugins/plugin-a
          - name: plugin-b
             source: ./plugins/plugin-b
    ```

2. Run command:

    ```bash
   apm marketplace audit example-marketplace --strict --verbose
    ```

3. See every plugin skipped as `unsupported_source` instead of being audited from the local working tree.

4. Observe that the command still exits `0` in `--strict` mode even when all plugins were skipped.

**Expected behavior**
For a marketplace authored from a local repo or monorepo, `apm marketplace audit` should read each local plugin's `apm.yml` and apply the same `dependencies.apm` checks it uses for remote plugin sources.

If local plugin sources are intentionally out of scope, the command should make that limitation explicit and `--strict` should not look like a successful verification when zero plugins were actually audited.

At minimum, a strict audit that skips every plugin should not silently succeed.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Windows
- Python Version: 3.9.16
- APM Version: 0.26.0

**Logs**
Local-source marketplace config excerpt:

```yaml
marketplace:
   packages:
      - name: plugin-a
         source: ./plugins/plugin-a
      - name: plugin-b
         source: ./plugins/plugin-b
```

Command:

```bash
apm marketplace audit example-marketplace --strict --verbose
```

Observed result:

```text
[>] Auditing marketplace 'example-marketplace'...
[i] Checking 2 plugins...

Audit Results:
   plugin-a: skipped (unsupported_source - plugin source is not an addressable github manifest)
   plugin-b: skipped (unsupported_source - plugin source is not an addressable github manifest)

[+] Summary: 0 clean, 0 bypass warnings, 2 skipped, 0 unverifiable errors
```

Exit code:

```text
0
```

issues.title: compile --clean deletes tracked AGENTS.md inside nested git worktrees
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm compile --clean` treats `AGENTS.md` files belonging to **other git worktrees** as orphans and deletes them, when those worktrees live in a directory under the repository root (a common layout, e.g. `<repo>/.worktrees/<branch>/`).

In our repo the deleted files are **tracked in git**, so every affected worktree silently gains uncommitted deletions:

```
+ Removed .worktrees/fix-tsconfig-jsonc/e2e/AGENTS.md
+ Removed .worktrees/fix-tsconfig-jsonc/packages/cli/AGENTS.md
+ Removed .worktrees/fix-tsconfig-jsonc/e2e/fixtures/application/AGENTS.md
```

```
$ cd .worktrees/fix-tsconfig-jsonc && git status --short
 D e2e/AGENTS.md
 D e2e/fixtures/application/AGENTS.md
 D packages/cli/AGENTS.md
```

This is not a one-off: with several worktrees checked out in parallel, any `apm compile --clean` from the main working tree wipes all of them, and an agent working inside one can commit the deletions without noticing.

## Cause

`src/apm_cli/compilation/distributed_compiler.py:817` (identical in v0.26.0 and v0.27.0):

```python
for agents_file in self.base_dir.rglob("AGENTS.md"):
    relative_path = agents_file.resolve().relative_to(self.base_dir.resolve())
    skip_dirs = {".git", ".apm", "node_modules", "__pycache__", ".pytest_cache", "apm_modules"}
    if any(part in skip_dirs for part in relative_path.parts):
        continue
```

A nested worktree is an independent checkout with its own generated `AGENTS.md` files carrying the APM marker, so they pass the marker gate and are removed.

There is currently no way to opt out:

- `skip_dirs` is a hardcoded literal.
- `.gitignore` is not consulted (our `.worktrees` entry has no effect).
- `apm.yml` has no corresponding key, `apm compile` has no corresponding flag, and there is no env var.
- `DistributedAgentsCompiler.__init__` does take `exclude_patterns`, but the CLI never passes it, and it feeds the project-structure analyzer (same file, :123) rather than the orphan scan.

## Suggested fix

A git worktree root is easy to detect: it contains a `.git` **file** (a gitdir pointer), not a `.git` directory. Skipping any directory whose root has that would fix this without new configuration:

```python
def _is_nested_worktree(path: Path) -> bool:
    return (path / ".git").is_file()
```

…and prune such directories during the walk. Alternatively (or additionally), honour an `excludes:` key in `apm.yml` for the orphan scan.

## Environment

- apm 0.26.0 (also verified the code is unchanged in v0.27.0), macOS arm64, PyInstaller build from the GitHub release
- Layout: main working tree at `<repo>`, additional `git worktree add` targets under `<repo>/.worktrees/<slug>`

## Workaround

Move worktrees outside the repository root so `base_dir.rglob(...)` cannot reach them, and keep `--clean` out of any automatically-run script (we had it in `package.json` `prepare`, which meant every `bun install` triggered it).

issues.title: [BUG] `apm marketplace add` does not recognize fully-qualified `ssh://` URLs
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm marketplace add` does not recognize a fully-qualified `ssh://` URL. The value is misclassified as `host/owner/repo`-style shorthand, so the leading `ssh:` segment ends up inside the owner/repo path (with a default host silently assumed) and surfaces as a mangled `ssh:/` in the error.

This matters most for servers that accept SSH only on a non-default port: the SCP-like shorthand (`git@host:org/repo.git`) that `apm marketplace add` does support cannot express a port, so the broken `ssh://host:port/...` form is the only apm-native syntax for that case — leaving no working syntax at all, short of external workarounds such as git's `insteadOf` rewrite (below) or an `ssh_config` host entry.

**To Reproduce**

The supplied host is never contacted, so this reproduces even against a nonexistent host — no real Git server needed:

```bash
$ apm --version
Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.27.0 (703dd9e)

$ apm marketplace add "ssh://git@nonexistent-host-test.invalid:2222/org/repo.git"
[*] Registering marketplace 'repo'...
[x] No marketplace.json found in 'ssh:/git@nonexistent-host-test.invalid:2222/org/repo'. Checked: marketplace.json, .github/plugin/marketplace.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
$ echo $?
1
```

The same command without the port fails identically, so this is not port-specific. For contrast, the forms `apm marketplace add` does recognize proceed to the network stage and fail there on hostname resolution, as expected for a nonexistent host:

```bash
$ apm marketplace add "git@nonexistent-host-test.invalid:org/repo.git"
[*] Registering marketplace 'repo'...
[x] Failed to register marketplace: Failed to fetch marketplace 'repo': git ls-remote failed for git@nonexistent-host-test.invalid:org/repo.git: ssh: Could not resolve hostname nonexistent-host-test.invalid ...
```

(`https://nonexistent-host-test.invalid/org/repo.git` likewise reaches `git ls-remote`. The `.git` suffix dropping in the first error is apm's own normalization, not a separate issue.)

**Expected behavior**

A fully-qualified `ssh://` URL (with or without a port) should be recognized as an SSH remote and reach the same `git ls-remote` stage that the SCP-like and `https://` forms reach.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS
- APM Version: 0.27.0 (703dd9e), via `apm --version`
- Installed via: Homebrew (`microsoft/apm` tap)

**Additional context**

_Root cause, from our own reading of the `v0.27.0` source (not maintainer-confirmed):_ `_parse_marketplace_source()` (`src/apm_cli/commands/marketplace/__init__.py`, lines 247-387) handles local paths, `file://`, SCP-like SSH, `https://`, and shorthand — there is no `ssh://` branch. An `ssh://` value falls into the shorthand `split("/")` path, where `ssh:` fails the FQDN host check (line 354) and becomes the leading owner-path segment, with `default_host()` (`github.com`) silently assumed (line 383) — consistent with the observed error. Three signs this is a gap rather than intended scope:

- Dependency resolution already supports `ssh://` with ports: `DependencyReference._parse_ssh_protocol_url()` (`src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py`, ~521-598).
- That same file even directs users to the `ssh://` form when an SCP path carries a port: "SCP shorthand can't carry a port. Use the ssh:// URL form instead" (~1370-1376).
- `marketplace add`'s own error text lists "an SSH URL" among the accepted forms (lines 346-351).

A possible direction is recognizing `ssh://` in `_parse_marketplace_source()` before the shorthand fallback, aligned with `_parse_ssh_protocol_url()` — but we defer to maintainers on the actual shape of the fix.

**Workaround** (verified on APM 0.27.0, macOS): rewrite at the git level and hand apm the `https://` form. Note this is a global git config change affecting all git operations on the machine:

```bash
git config --global url."ssh://git@git-server.example.com:2222/".insteadOf "https://git-server.example.com/"
apm marketplace add https://git-server.example.com/org/repo.git
```

**Related**: [PR #1476](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/pull/1476) (Merged) added SCP-like SSH support, but its enumerated accepted forms do not include `ssh://` URLs; [#2063](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/2063) / [PR #2091](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/pull/2091) (Merged) preserve a registered SSH transport in dependency resolution, but don't touch `marketplace add`'s URL parsing.

---

_Disclosure: this report was drafted with AI assistance; all commands, outputs, and the workaround above were run and verified manually on the environment described._

issues.title: [BUG] opencode target emits schema-invalid agents (tools as list, unresolved model names, non-opencode tool vocabulary)
issues.body:
## Summary

When compiling agents for the `opencode` target, apm emits
`.opencode/agents/*.md` whose frontmatter does not conform to OpenCode's agent
schema:

1. **`tools` is rendered as a YAML list** (e.g.
   `tools: ['read', 'edit', 'search', 'execute', 'todo']`), but OpenCode
   requires `tools` to be a map `Record<string, boolean>` (tool-name ->
   enabled). A list fails schema decoding, so the intended tool grants are
   dropped and the agent gets the default tool set.
2. **`model` is rendered as a display name** (e.g.
   `model: Claude Sonnet 5 (copilot)`), but OpenCode resolves `model` as a
   `provider/model` identifier. Display names don't resolve, so the agent falls
   back to the default model.
3. **Tool names use the source/Copilot vocabulary** (`vscode`, `execute`,
   `todo`, `agent`, and namespaced MCP tools like `<server>/*`) rather than
   OpenCode's tool names (`bash`, `read`, `edit`, `write`, `grep`, `glob`,
   `webfetch`, `task`, ...). Even once formatted as a map, these grant/deny
   tools OpenCode does not have.

Net effect: every generated OpenCode agent loads with the wrong (default) model
and without its intended tool restrictions.

## Environment

- apm 0.26.0 and 0.27.0.
- Source agents defined once (harness-neutral) and compiled to multiple targets
  including `opencode`.
- All generated OpenCode agents affected.

## Reproduction

1. Configure `targets: [copilot, claude, opencode]` (or
   `apm compile --target opencode`).
2. `apm install` (or `apm compile`).
3. Inspect any `.opencode/agents/*.md` frontmatter.

Observed frontmatter (example):

```yaml
---
name: SomeAgent
model: Claude Sonnet 5 (copilot)
target: vscode
user-invocable: false
tools:
  ['read', 'edit', 'search', 'execute', 'todo', 'vscode']
---
```

## Expected (per OpenCode agent schema)

```yaml
---
name: SomeAgent
description: ...
mode: subagent
model: github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5   # provider/model id
tools:
  read: true
  edit: true
  bash: true
  webfetch: true
---
```

- `tools` as `Record<string, boolean>`.
- `model` as a resolvable `provider/model` id.
- Tool names mapped to OpenCode's vocabulary (unmappable source tools dropped
  rather than passed through verbatim).
- Non-schema keys such as `target` / `user-invocable` dropped (OpenCode ignores
  unknown keys, but they are noise).

## Reference

OpenCode agent config schema (sst/opencode,
`packages/core/src/v1/config/agent.ts`):

```
tools: Schema.optional(Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Boolean))
model: Schema.optional(Schema.String)   // resolved as provider/model
```

## Notes

This looks like vendor-to-vendor passthrough rather than translation to
OpenCode's semantic model -- likely related to the OpenAPM translation work
(#2112 / #2109). Happy to provide full sample files.

issues.title: [BUG] Plugin LSP servers declared with `fileExtensions` are silently skipped (official dotnet plugin)
issues.body:
Installing the official dotnet plugin (`apm install dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet`) deploys its skill but silently drops the LSP server it ships. That plugin's headline feature is the C# language server integration, so what actually lands is missing the main thing.

Repro:

```
apm install dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet
```

Expected: the `csharp` server from the plugin's lsp.json ends up in `.lsp.json` / `.github/lsp.json`, per the docs (plugin LSP servers "are automatically extracted and integrated").

Actual: only the skill deploys. No `lsp_servers` in apm.lock.yaml, nothing in the runtime configs. The skip warning is only visible in verbose mode.

Cause: the plugin's lsp.json declares the extension map as `fileExtensions`, but `LSPDependency` validation requires `extensionToLanguage`, so `_lsp_servers_to_apm_deps` in `src/apm_cli/deps/plugin_parser.py` rejects the server as invalid and skips it. The odd part: apm itself writes `fileExtensions` when generating the Copilot CLI output, so the intake path rejects the exact spelling the output path produces — and that the official dotnet plugin uses.

Suggestion: accept `fileExtensions` as an input alias for `extensionToLanguage` in the plugin parser (and possibly map the plugin's `warmupTimeoutMs` to `startupTimeout` while at it). dotnet/skills renaming their field would also fix this one plugin, but apm tolerating both spellings seems more robust given both exist in the wild.

Workaround that works today: hand-author the server as a full object under `dependencies.lsp:` in apm.yml with the `extensionToLanguage` spelling.

apm 0.27.0 on Windows 11.

*Disclosure: drafted with AI assistance; the behavior was reproduced and verified manually.*

issues.title: [FEATURE] Support the Agent Plugins 1.0 spec in `apm pack`
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`apm pack --format plugin` emits a different manifest per ecosystem. In `build_plugin_manifest`, Claude keeps `mcpServers` while Copilot has it stripped, and components are declared through explicit path fields. That per-client branching is the duplication [Agent Plugins 1.0](https://agent-plugins.org/) removes.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Emit a spec-conformant package:

* `$schema` set to `https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json`
* Skills under `skills/`, MCP servers in root `mcp.json` (not `.mcp.json` or inline `mcpServers`)
* Components discovered from fixed locations rather than manifest path fields
* Anything client-specific moved under a reverse-domain key in `extensions`

Clients supporting the spec then load one package without per-ecosystem variants.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Keeping the current per-ecosystem output. It works, but the branching grows with every client APM targets, and spec support is already shipping across clients.

**Additional context**

* [Specification](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/spec/1.0.0.md)
* [Example plugin and migration guide](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-example)
* Existing manifest generation: `src/apm_cli/core/plugin_manifest.py`
* Related: #1597, #225

issues.title: [BUG] --skill matches nothing on subdirectory plugin refs: 'Available: (none)'
issues.body:
Subsetting skills works for repo-root plugin packages but fails for subdirectory plugin refs — the skill enumeration comes back empty, so any `--skill` value is rejected.

Repro:

```
apm install dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced --skill csharp-scripts
```

Output:

```
[x] 1 package failed:
  +- dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced -- --skill matched no declared skills in
'dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced'. Requested: csharp-scripts. Available: (none).
[x] Installation failed with 1 error(s). No install transaction changes were committed.
```

The skill definitely exists: a bare `apm install dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced` deploys `csharp-scripts` (plus `dotnet-pinvoke` and `nuget-trusted-publishing`) fine — it's the subset matching that can't see any skills. The package resolves as `package_type: marketplace_plugin` with a virtual subdirectory path.

For comparison, `apm install DuendeSoftware/duende-skills --skill ...` (a repo-root plugin) subsets correctly, so this looks specific to the subdirectory-ref intake path not feeding the enumerator that `--skill` validates against.

Expected: `--skill` filters subdirectory plugin refs the same way it does repo-root packages, persisting the `skills:` subset in apm.yml.

apm 0.27.0 on Windows 11.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-08-10
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-10
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (3aa0365)
**Commands Inspected**: 33 top-level + all subcommands (approx. 60 help invocations total)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm install --target` docs missing supported targets

- **Command**: `apm install --target`
- **Problem**: The `install` reference docs list targets as: `copilot`, `claude`, `grok-build`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `codex`, `gemini`, `antigravity`, `windsurf`, `kiro`, `intellij`, `vscode`, `agent-skills`, `all`. The actual CLI accepts four additional target values that are entirely absent from the docs: `agents`, `agy`, `hermes`, `openclaw`. (The docs do separately mention `vscode` and `agents` as deprecated aliases in the `compile` reference, but not in `install`.)
- **Evidence**:
  - Actual CLI: `apm install --help` shows `agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude, codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork, cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-cloud, hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf`
  - Docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md` line 49): `copilot, claude, grok-build, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, intellij, vscode, agent-skills, all` -- `agents`, `agy`, `hermes`, and `openclaw` are absent
  - Same omission exists in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md`
- **Suggested Fix**: Add the missing targets to the `--target` table in both `install.md` and `update.md`. Annotate `agents` and `vscode` as deprecated aliases for `copilot` (as already done in `compile.md` line 73), and `agy` as an alias for `antigravity`. Document `hermes` and `openclaw` as supported targets.

---

#### `--parallel-checks` default value format inconsistent with `--parallel-downloads`

- **Command**: `apm outdated`
- **Problem**: The `--parallel-checks` flag renders its default inline in the help description string instead of using Click's `show_default=True`, producing a different visual style compared to every other parallelism flag in the CLI.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm outdated --help`: `-j, --parallel-checks INTEGER  Max concurrent remote checks (default: 4, 0 = sequential)`
  - `apm install --help`:  `--parallel-downloads INTEGER  Max concurrent package downloads (0 to disable parallelism)  [default: 4]`
  - `apm update --help`:   `--parallel-downloads INTEGER  Max concurrent package downloads (0 to disable parallelism)  [default: 4]`
  - Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/outdated.py` uses `help="Max concurrent remote checks (default: 4, 0 = sequential)"` without `show_default=True`, unlike install/update which use `show_default=True`
- **Suggested Fix**: In `src/apm_cli/commands/outdated.py`, change the `--parallel-checks` option to use `show_default=True` and move `(0 = sequential)` into the help string, e.g.: `help="Max concurrent remote checks (0 = sequential)"` with `show_default=True`. This produces `[default: 4]` at the end, matching the other commands.

---

#### `apm compile --all` help text omits deprecation of `--target all`

- **Command**: `apm compile --all`
- **Problem**: The CLI help text for `--all` says "Equivalent to --target all" without noting that `--target all` is deprecated in favor of `--all`. A user reading the help might use `--target all` without knowing it will emit a deprecation warning. The docs do explain this correctly.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm compile --help`: `--all  Compile for all canonical targets. Equivalent to --target all.`
  - `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/compile.md` line 74-75: "`--target all` also emits a deprecation warning -- prefer `--all`."
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--all` help string to: `"Compile for all canonical targets. Equivalent to --target all (deprecated form; prefer --all)."` or similar wording so the inline help reflects the deprecation.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm config list` description slightly misleading

- **Command**: `apm config list`
- **Problem**: The CLI help says "List all configuration values" but the command actually prints a filtered summary of core user-settable keys (same as `apm config get` with no argument), not every possible configuration value. The docs correctly describe it as "Alias for `apm config get` with no argument."
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm config list --help`: `List all configuration values`
  - `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/config.md`: "`apm config list` -- Alias for `apm config get` with no argument; produces the same user config summary."
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the CLI description to: "Show a summary of user-settable configuration values (alias for 'apm config get')."

---

#### `apm deps update` stale `--target` value list (deprecated command)

- **Command**: `apm deps update --target`
- **Problem**: The deprecated `apm deps update` command advertises a shorter target list (`copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all`) compared to the current equivalents (`apm update`, `apm install`), which include `hermes`, `openclaw`, `agy`, `vscode`, `agents`, `grok-build`, `grok-cloud`, `intellij`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`. Since the command is deprecated, this inconsistency is low risk, but users who haven't migrated may be confused.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm deps update --help --target`: shows only 11 values
  - `apm update --help --target`: shows 21 values
- **Suggested Fix**: Either update `deps update` to use the shared target constant, or add a note to its help text explaining the target list is not current and users should migrate to `apm update`.

---

### Clean Areas

The following areas passed all consistency checks with no issues found:

- **Command coverage**: All 33 top-level commands are fully documented with a matching reference page in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`.
- **Error handling**: All tested invalid-input cases (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no arg, `apm config set` with no args, `apm mcp search` with no arg) produce clean, non-traceback error messages with a "Try ... --help" pointer.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works correctly on every command and subcommand tested.
- **`--verbose` / `-v`**: Present and consistently named across all commands that support it.
- **`--dry-run`**: Present on all commands that perform mutating operations (`install`, `update`, `compile`, `deps clean`, `uninstall`, `unpack`, `prune`, `audit`).
- **`--yes` / `-y`**: Present on `update` and `deps clean` where confirmation prompts exist.
- **`-g, --global`**: Consistently named and described across `deps list`, `deps tree`, `deps update`, `install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `outdated`, `lock`, `compile`.
- **Subcommand structure**: `deps`, `mcp`, `config`, `runtime`, `cache`, `experimental`, `marketplace`, `lifecycle`, `plugin`, `policy` all expose logical subcommand groups with sensible descriptions.
- **`apm mcp` list/search defaults**: `apm mcp list --limit` defaults to 20 (matches docs); `apm mcp search --limit` defaults to 10 (matches docs).
- **`apm config unset`**: Present in CLI and correctly documented.
- **`apm runtime` subcommands**: `list`, `setup`, `status`, `remove` all present and documented.

issues.title: [aw] No-Op Runs
issues.body:
This issue tracks all no-op runs from agentic workflows in this repository. Each workflow run that completes with a no-op message (indicating no action was needed) posts a comment here.

<details>
<summary>What is a No-Op?</summary>

A no-op (no operation) occurs when an agentic workflow runs successfully but determines that no action is required. For example:
- A security scanner that finds no issues
- An update checker that finds nothing to update
- A monitoring workflow that finds everything is healthy

These are successful outcomes, not failures, and help provide transparency into workflow behavior.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How This Helps</summary>

This issue helps you:
- Track workflows that ran but determined no action was needed
- Distinguish between failures and intentional no-ops
- Monitor workflow health by seeing when workflows decide not to act

</details>

<details>
