issues.title: [BUG] `apm install PACKAGE --dry-run` omits the new package from its plan on 0.28.0
issues.body:
## Summary When a package is passed positionally to `apm install --dry-run`, APM 0.28.0 validates it and reports that it would add one package to `apm.yml`. The displayed installation plan then says that `apm.yml` contains no dependencies, and the final summary says that no changes would be installed. The command exits successfully. This makes the preview internally contradictory and prevents it from serving as a reliable review step before an install. ## Prerequisites - A POSIX `sh` environment with Git available - APM CLI exactly 0.28.0 on `PATH` - HTTPS access to the public `microsoft/apm-sample-package` repository; no credentials are required ## Reproduction The package reference below is pinned to commit `fb2851683be0e0e7711421d518bd8dba23b0b1f6`. The script retains its temporary workspace for inspection and exits zero only when all contradictory parts of the preview are present. ```sh #!/bin/sh set -eux PACKAGE='microsoft/apm-sample-package#fb2851683be0e0e7711421d518bd8dba23b0b1f6' REPRO_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/apm-install-dry-run-XXXXXX") if ! command -v apm >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'apm is not on PATH' >&2 exit 1 fi APM_VERSION=$(apm --version 2>&1) case "$APM_VERSION" in *'version 0.28.0'*) ;; *) echo "expected APM 0.28.0; got: $APM_VERSION" >&2 exit 1 ;; esac echo "Workspace: $REPRO_DIR" cd "$REPRO_DIR" apm init -y --target agent-skills . >/dev/null if apm install "$PACKAGE" --no-policy --dry-run >actual.log 2>&1; then : else install_status=$? cat actual.log >&2 echo "apm install unexpectedly exited $install_status" >&2 exit 1 fi cat actual.log awk ' /Dry run mode - showing what would be installed:/ { in_plan = 1 } in_plan { print } /Dry run complete - no changes made/ { exit } ' actual.log >plan.log grep -F 'Dry run: Would add 1 package(s) to apm.yml' actual.log >/dev/null grep -F 'Dry run mode - showing what would be installed:' plan.log >/dev/null grep -F 'No dependencies found in apm.yml' plan.log >/dev/null grep -F 'would install no changes' actual.log >/dev/null if grep -F "$PACKAGE" plan.log >/dev/null; then echo 'package unexpectedly appeared in the displayed plan' >&2 exit 1 fi echo "Reproduced; workspace retained at: $REPRO_DIR" ``` ## Actual behavior The package is accepted, but the plan is calculated without it: ```text Dry run: Would add 1 package(s) to apm.yml Installing 1 new package... Dry run mode - showing what would be installed: No dependencies found in apm.yml Dry run complete - no changes made Dry run completed: would install no changes in 0.1s. ``` The immutable package coordinate appears in validation output before the plan, but not in the plan block itself.
Possibly related: migrating a local dependency into .apm/skills A separate migration case may point to the same plan-construction boundary. After an installed local skill is moved into the root package's `.apm/skills/` directory and removed from `dependencies.apm`, a bare dry run lists its deployed paths as removals, omits the root package integration, and still concludes that it would install no changes. This observation is not required to reproduce the positional-package failure above. The following script creates the prior installed state, performs only the source and manifest migration, and exits zero only for the contradictory preview: ```sh #!/bin/sh set -eux REPRO_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/apm-root-skill-dry-run-XXXXXX") if ! command -v apm >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'apm is not on PATH' >&2 exit 1 fi APM_VERSION=$(apm --version 2>&1) case "$APM_VERSION" in *'version 0.28.0'*) ;; *) echo "expected APM 0.28.0; got: $APM_VERSION" >&2 exit 1 ;; esac echo "Workspace: $REPRO_DIR" cd "$REPRO_DIR" mkdir -p skills/example cat >skills/example/SKILL.md <<'MARKDOWN' --- name: example description: A minimal project-owned skill used to reproduce an APM dry-run issue. --- # Example Return the word `example`. MARKDOWN cat >apm.yml <<'YAML' name: apm-root-skill-dry-run-repro version: 0.1.0 description: Reproduce root skill dry-run behavior targets: - agent-skills dependencies: apm: - path: ./skills/example mcp: [] includes: auto scripts: {} YAML apm install --no-policy >baseline.log 2>&1 test -f .agents/skills/example/SKILL.md mkdir -p .apm/skills mv skills/example .apm/skills/example rmdir skills cat >apm.yml <<'YAML' name: apm-root-skill-dry-run-repro version: 0.1.0 description: Reproduce root skill dry-run behavior targets: - agent-skills dependencies: apm: [] mcp: [] includes: auto scripts: {} YAML cksum \ apm.yml \ apm.lock.yaml \ .apm/skills/example/SKILL.md \ .agents/skills/example/SKILL.md >before.cksum if apm install --no-policy --dry-run >actual.log 2>&1; then : else install_status=$? cat actual.log >&2 echo "apm install unexpectedly exited $install_status" >&2 exit 1 fi cat actual.log grep -F 'No dependencies found in apm.yml' actual.log >/dev/null grep -F 'Files that would be removed' actual.log >/dev/null grep -F '.agents/skills/example' actual.log >/dev/null grep -F 'would install no changes' actual.log >/dev/null if grep -F '' actual.log >/dev/null || \ grep -F 'skill(s) integrated' actual.log >/dev/null; then echo 'root package integration unexpectedly appeared in the plan' >&2 exit 1 fi test -f .agents/skills/example/SKILL.md cksum \ apm.yml \ apm.lock.yaml \ .apm/skills/example/SKILL.md \ .agents/skills/example/SKILL.md >after.cksum cmp before.cksum after.cksum echo "Reproduced; workspace retained at: $REPRO_DIR" ``` The relevant preview is: ```text Dry run mode - showing what would be installed: No dependencies found in apm.yml Files that would be removed (packages no longer in apm.yml): 2 - .agents/skills/example - .agents/skills/example/SKILL.md Dry run complete - no changes made Dry run completed: would install no changes in 0.0s. ```
## Expected behavior The dry-run plan should include the validated positional package and show that it would be installed. Its final summary should report one prospective install while leaving the manifest, lockfile, and deployment unchanged. ## References - [APM v0.28.0](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/releases/tag/v0.28.0) - [`install.py` reports the validated dry-run additions](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/e041462f4a48086dbee3da145c07d71b8a3b84fd/src/apm_cli/commands/install.py#L675-L682) - [`dry_run.py` renders dependencies from the existing manifest](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/e041462f4a48086dbee3da145c07d71b8a3b84fd/src/apm_cli/install/presentation/dry_run.py#L32-L57) - [Pinned public package used by the reproducer](https://github.com/microsoft/apm-sample-package/tree/fb2851683be0e0e7711421d518bd8dba23b0b1f6)

issues.title: Remaining platform-native text writers: 'apm pack' output is not cross-OS reproducible; project-file writers flip-flop line endings on Windows
issues.body:
## Context

#2619 (fix: #2620) established the invariant that **every file APM writes into a hashed package tree must be LF-deterministic**, and fixed the in-tree writers (synthetic `apm.yml`, inline-hooks `hooks.json`, `dump_yaml`). An exhaustive audit of the remaining platform-native text writes found two sibling groups that are real but out of that PR's scope. Filing them so they don't get lost.

## 1. Bundle export / pack output is not cross-platform reproducible

These sites write **generated** text with `Path.write_text()` (platform newline translation — CRLF on Windows):

- `src/apm_cli/bundle/plugin_exporter.py:990` — merged `hooks.json`
- `src/apm_cli/bundle/plugin_exporter.py:996` — merged `.mcp.json`
- `src/apm_cli/bundle/plugin_exporter.py:1003` — generated `plugin.json`
- `src/apm_cli/bundle/plugin_exporter.py:1035` — enriched `apm.lock.yaml`
- `src/apm_cli/bundle/packer.py:318` — enriched `apm.lock.yaml`
- `src/apm_cli/core/plugin_manifest.py:463` — generated `plugin.json`

Consequence: a bundle packed on Windows is byte- and hash-different from the same bundle packed on Linux. Each artifact is internally self-consistent, so the break surfaces when a publisher repacks the same version on a different OS — consuming lockfiles pinning the old `content_hash` fail verification. Fix is mechanical: route through `apm_cli.utils.atomic_io.write_text_lf` / `atomic_write_text`.

## 2. Project-file YAML writers still platform-native → line-ending flip-flop on Windows

After #2620, `yaml_io.dump_yaml` writes LF, but its two siblings still write platform-native:

- `dump_yaml_roundtrip` (`src/apm_cli/utils/yaml_io.py`, `open()` without `newline=""`) — used by `install/package_resolution.py`, `commands/install.py`, `commands/uninstall/cli.py` to rewrite the **project** `apm.yml`
- `write_yaml_text_atomic` (`src/apm_cli/utils/yaml_io.py`, `os.fdopen` without `newline=""`) — used by `deps/revision_pins.py`

On Windows this makes the project `apm.yml` line endings flip-flop between consecutive commands (`apm install` → CRLF via roundtrip writer; `apm mcp add` / `apm lifecycle init` → LF via `dump_yaml`), producing whole-file git diff churn. None of these files are content-hashed, so this is hygiene rather than a lockfile-portability bug — but any **future** hashed-tree caller of either writer would silently reintroduce the #2619 class. Making both writers LF-deterministic closes the class; note it changes the on-disk bytes of user-committed files on Windows once (git `autocrlf` absorbs it).

## Non-goals

- `compute_package_hash` must keep hashing raw bytes (see its docstring — normalizing there would invalidate existing correct lockfiles).

Refs: #1952, #2187, #2223, #2619, #2620.

issues.title: Add Kilo Code as a compile/install target
issues.body:
## Feature request

Add **Kilo Code** as a supported target for `apm compile` / `apm install`, alongside `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `grok-build`, `copilot`, `opencode`, `windsurf`, and `kiro`.

- **Target slug:** `kilo`
- **Deploy root (project):** `.kilo/`
- **Detection signal:** `.kilo/` directory (distinct from existing `kiro` target's `.kiro/`)

## Target mapping

Sources: [skills](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/skills), [subagents](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-subagents), [custom-modes](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-modes), [AGENTS.md](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/agents-md), [custom-instructions](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-instructions), [MCP](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/mcp/using-in-kilo-code).

| Primitive | Global (user) | Project |
|---|---|---|
| Instructions (`AGENTS.md`) | `~/.config/kilo/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` (root and distributed subdirectories) |
| Skills (`SKILL.md` trees) | `~/.agents/skills/` (shared) | `.agents/skills/` (shared) |
| Agents | `~/.config/kilo/agents/*.md` | `.kilo/agents/*.md` |
| Prompts / Commands | `~/.config/kilo/commands/*.md` | `.kilo/commands/*.md` |
| MCP Servers | `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` | `.kilo/kilo.jsonc` |

- **Instructions:** Kilo reads root + per-directory `AGENTS.md` ([agents-md](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/agents-md)). `apm compile` → `AGENTS.md` (`agents` family, distributed by default per `applyTo:` globs); `apm compile -g` → `~/.config/kilo/AGENTS.md` ([custom-instructions](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-instructions)).
- **Skills:** Standard Agent Skills format — folder + `SKILL.md` with `name`, `description` frontmatter. Reuses the shared `.agents/skills/` path (following `opencode` / `codex` conventions) as Kilo scans `.agents/skills/` by default ([skills](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/skills)).
- **Agents:** Markdown + YAML frontmatter; body is system prompt; filename (minus `.md`) = agent name ([custom-modes](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-modes)).
- **Prompts / Commands:** Markdown workflow files located in `.kilo/commands/*.md` ([workflows](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/agent-manager-workflows)).
- **MCP Servers:** Configured under the top-level `"mcp"` key in `kilo.jsonc` ([using-in-kilo-code](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/mcp/using-in-kilo-code)).

### Notes on user-scope paths (`.config` used only where no alternative exists)

- **Global skills:** Follows `opencode` / `codex` convention and targets `~/.agents/skills/` ([skills](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/skills)).
- **Global agents, commands, and instructions:** Currently have no Home-relative documented location — all live in `~/.config/kilo/` ([subagents](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-subagents), [custom-instructions](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-instructions)).

## Key facts

1. **Skills reuse `.agents/skills/`:** Kilo automatically scans `EXTERNAL_DIRS = [".claude", ".agents"]` → `~/.agents/skills/` (global) and `.agents/skills/**/SKILL.md` up the project tree ([skills](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/skills)). APM's existing `.agents/skills/` deploy is picked up without requiring duplicate deployments to `.kilo/skills/`.
2. **Agents require native deployment:** Agent files are discovered from `.kilo/agents/` (project) and `~/.config/kilo/agents/` (global) ([subagents](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-subagents)).
3. **MCP integration:** `apm install --mcp` writes server configurations to `.kilo/kilo.jsonc` (bootstrapping the file if it does not exist) or `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` at global scope.

## Registration

- Add `kilo` to `apm.yml` `targets:` validation, `apm targets` table, and `--target` / `--all` catalog (non-explicit ⇒ included in `all`).
- Targets matrix: project root `.kilo/`; `instructions` via `AGENTS.md`; `agents` → `.kilo/agents/*.md`; `prompts` → `.kilo/commands/*.md`; `skills` → reused `.agents/skills/`; `mcp` → `.kilo/kilo.jsonc`.
- User-scope compile → `~/.config/kilo/AGENTS.md`.
- Tests mirroring `opencode` / `kiro` target tests.

## Config / env surface

- Config: global `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` (Windows `C:\Users\<user>\.config\kilo\kilo.jsonc`), project `./.kilo/kilo.jsonc` or `./kilo.jsonc` ([settings](https://kilo.ai/docs/getting-started/settings), [CLI](https://kilo.ai/docs/cli)).
- Extra skill dirs: `skills.paths` / `skills.urls` in `kilo.jsonc`.
- Env overrides: `KILO_CONFIG`, `KILO_CONFIG_DIR`, `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT`, `KILO_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS` ([CLI](https://kilo.ai/docs/cli), [architecture](https://kilo.ai/docs/contributing/architecture/cli-runtime)).

## Testing

- `.kilo/` activates `kilo`; no collision with `.kiro/`.
- `apm compile -t kilo` → `AGENTS.md` (root and distributed); `apm compile -g` → `~/.config/kilo/AGENTS.md`.
- `apm install -t kilo` → `.kilo/agents/*.md`, `.kilo/commands/*.md`, and skills via `.agents/skills/`.
- `apm install --mcp <name> -t kilo` → writes to `.kilo/kilo.jsonc` (bootstrapped if absent).
- `apm targets --json` lists `kilo`.
- Manual verification: `kilo` CLI picks up skills, subagents, commands, and MCP servers.

issues.title: [perf-scan] 2026-08-23 -- performance opportunities found
issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-08-23

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [B] Linear scan inside nested loop -- security/executables.py:267-288 and 747-755

- Current: O(K * E * C * G) -- `_map_grants` iterates all entries of each grant_map
  dict (O(G)) including calling `_strip_version(stored_key)` per entry. Called C=4-6
  times per `resolve_exec_decision`, which is itself called inside a nested loop:
  `for key in candidate_keys: for exec_type in ALL_EXEC_TYPES` (lines 747-755) and
  a second nested loop at lines 779-782. K=candidate_keys, E=exec_types (~4),
  G=grant_map size.
- Proposed: O(K * E) after O(G) pre-build -- build a
  `{stripped_key: {exec_type: bool}}` index from each grant_map (user_allow,
  user_deny, project_allow, project_deny) once before the outer loop.
- Fix: In `_map_grants`, add an optional pre-built normalized-key index parameter;
  before the outer `for key in candidate_keys` loop, call a helper that produces
  `dict[str, dict[str, bool]]` keyed by `_strip_version(stored_key)` for each
  grant_map, then replace the linear scan with an O(1) dict lookup.

#### [B] O(n*m) prefix scan on deployed files -- bundle/lockfile_enrichment.py:151

- Current: O(n * m) -- `[f for f in deployed_files if any(f.startswith(p) for p
  in prefixes)]` iterates all deployed files (n) and for each file checks all
  target prefixes (m) until a match is found. Called during `apm pack` and bundle
  export operations.
- Proposed: O(n * log(m)) or amortised O(n) -- sort `prefixes` once and use
  `bisect` to find the longest candidate prefix per file, or group files by
  common prefix using a trie-like dict keyed on the first path segment.
- Fix: Sort `prefixes` by length descending once before the comprehension and
  break early; for large deployments, build a `{first_segment: [prefixes]}` dict
  to skip non-matching prefixes in O(1) per file. Low-priority: m is typically
  10-20 entries, so the fix matters mainly for deployments with hundreds of files.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (445 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [BUG] Private GitHub subdirectory installs bypass credential-aware persistent cache
issues.body:
## Description

Persistent caching of a private GitHub subdirectory package bypasses APM's credential fallback. The cache attempt is forced through the anonymous GitHub environment, fails authentication, emits a misleading filter-v2 warning, and is discarded. Installation then succeeds through the normal authenticated download path.

Tested with APM 0.28.0 and current `main` (0.29.0) on macOS arm64.

## Reproduction

1. Create a private GitHub repository containing an installable APM package in a subdirectory.
2. Confirm that an HTTPS Git clone succeeds non-interactively through the configured credential helper.
3. Install the subdirectory package:

```console
apm install --target skills OWNER/PRIVATE_REPO/path/to/package#TAG
```

APM emits:

```text
Partial clone (--filter=blob:none) failed for https://github.com/OWNER/PRIVATE_REPO; retrying with full bare clone. Server may not support filter v2.
```

Installation succeeds through a later path, but `apm cache info` reports no cached Git repository/checkout for the package. Installing several subdirectory packages repeats the same failed cache attempt and warning.

## Root cause evidence

The same filtered bare clone succeeds when normal Git credential helpers are available.

In current `main`, `GitHubPackageDownloader._cache_git_env()` chooses `build_public_github_anonymous_git_env()` for `github.com` before repository privacy is known. That environment suppresses credential helpers and retains `GIT_ASKPASS=echo`. `GitCache._ensure_bare_repo()` interprets every partial-clone `CalledProcessError` as possible filter-v2 incompatibility and retries a full clone with the same anonymous environment. Both attempts fail authentication; the downloader catches the cache exception and continues through its normal authenticated path.

Removing `GIT_ASKPASS` from the anonymous cache environment changes the low-level error to:

```text
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled
```

This demonstrates an authentication-path failure, not filter-v2 incompatibility.

## Expected behavior

- After an anonymous cache attempt receives an authentication-equivalent failure, retry the persistent-cache operation through APM's existing credential resolution/fallback path.
- Only describe filter-v2 incompatibility when the failure supports that diagnosis; otherwise preserve an accurate sanitized diagnostic.
- Keep credentials out of argv, logs, persisted remote URLs, and cache keys.

## Impact

Installation remains functional, but private subdirectory packages cannot benefit from the persistent Git cache. Catalog operations repeat unnecessary network work and emit misleading warnings.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Load marketplace configuration directly from apm.yml
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Marketplace metadata and package entries can be declared in `apm.yml`, but `apm marketplace add` cannot consume that configuration directly. Authors must first run `apm pack --force` to generate `.github/plugin/marketplace.json`, then register the generated file separately.

This creates an unnecessary two-step workflow during local development and can cause the generated manifest to become stale relative to `apm.yml`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Allow APM to load a marketplace declaration directly from an `apm.yml` file, for example:

```text
apm marketplace add ./apm.yml --name example-marketplace
```

When the file contains a `marketplace` section, APM should resolve package sources relative to the `apm.yml` location and register the resulting marketplace without requiring a generated `marketplace.json` first. Existing workflows that consume a generated manifest or repository should continue to work unchanged.

APM should provide a clear validation error when the supplied `apm.yml` does not contain a usable `marketplace` declaration.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Continue running `apm pack --force`, then register `./.github/plugin/marketplace.json`.
- Register a repository URL and rely on its generated marketplace manifest.
- Edit the generated `marketplace.json` manually, which risks losing changes on the next build and conflicts with generated-file ownership.

**Additional context**

`apm.yml` is already the source configuration for marketplace metadata and package entries, while `.github/plugin/marketplace.json` is generated output. Direct loading would make the authoring source usable without weakening the generated-manifest workflow used for publishing and CI validation.

issues.title: [FEATURE] : support applyTo overrides for dependency instructions in apm.yml
issues.body:
### **Is Your Feature Request Related to a Problem? Please Describe.**

Consuming projects often use different repository and directory structures (e.g., monorepos, `apps/frontend/`, `lib/`, `pkg/`), but instructions from APM package dependencies come with hardcoded
  `applyTo` glob patterns (e.g., `src/**/*.ts`). Currently, consumers cannot adapt these imported instructions to their local layout without duplicating them locally, which quickly causes instructions
  to drift when the upstream package is updated.

### **Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow consuming projects to override or append `applyTo` patterns for specific dependency instructions directly in `apm.yml`.

    For example, supporting an overrides/mapping section under dependency declarations:

    ```yaml
    dependencies:
      apm:
        - name: "@org/ts-conventions"
          version: "^1.0.0"
          overrides:
            instructions:
              "ts-style":
                # Replace entirely or append to upstream applyTo
                applyTo: "apps/**/*.{ts,tsx},packages/**/*.{ts,tsx}"
                # or append: ["apps/**/*.ts"]

  When APM compiles/integrates targets (e.g., Cursor, Claude, Antigravity, Copilot), it should use the merged/overridden applyTo patterns instead of the upstream package defaults.

### **Describe alternatives you've considered**
1. Local Instruction Duplication: Copying the upstream instruction to .apm/instructions/ with custom applyTo globs. (Rejected: Leads to silent drift and loses automatic upstream updates.)
  2. Forking the Package: Maintaining a dedicated fork of the dependency for each repository layout. (Rejected: High maintenance burden and defeats the purpose of shared reusable APM packages.)
  
### **Additional context**
  This would greatly improve the reusability of shared APM packages across diverse codebases and monorepo architectures without compromising package maintenance.

issues.title: [BUG] apm compile silently overwrites hand-authored root CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (data loss)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Project-scope `apm compile` overwrites a hand-authored root context file with generated content. No marker check, no warning, no backup, exit 0.

`apm compile --global` has exactly this protection -- it logs `[i] claude: skipped (hand-authored) ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and leaves the file alone. Project scope has no equivalent, so the same hand-authored file is safe at user scope and destroyed at project scope.

This is the common case: a repo with a hand-written `CLAUDE.md` that later adopts APM. The first `apm compile` eats it.

**To Reproduce**

```bash
mkdir -p /private/tmp/apm-clobber/.apm/instructions && cd /private/tmp/apm-clobber
printf 'name: p\nversion: 1.0.0\ntargets: [claude, codex]\ndependencies:\n  apm: []\n  mcp: []\n' > apm.yml
printf -- '---\ndescription: standards\n---\n# Standards\nUS English.\n' > .apm/instructions/std.instructions.md
printf '# CLAUDE.md\n\nHAND-AUTHORED PROJECT MEMORY.\n' > CLAUDE.md
printf '# AGENTS.md\n\nHAND-AUTHORED.\n' > AGENTS.md
apm compile
cat CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
```

**Expected behavior**

Match the documented `--global` contract: "Hand-authored files (files that do not carry the APM-generated marker) are never overwritten." Skip the file and log it, or require an explicit `--force`. `apm compile --clean` already documents that it never deletes hand-authored files; the write path should honor the same rule.

**Actual behavior**

Both files are replaced by generated content and the original text is unrecoverable:

```
# CLAUDE.md
<!-- Generated by APM CLI -->
<!-- Build ID: 2bafa08f1415 -->

## Project Standards

### Global Instructions

# Standards
US English.
```

```
# AGENTS.md
<!-- Generated by APM CLI from distributed .apm/ primitives -->
<!-- Build ID: fa4413576225 -->

## Global Instructions

# Standards
US English.
```

`apm compile --root ~/.claude --target claude` is the same bug with a worse blast radius: it destroys the user's global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0)
- APM Version: 0.29.0 (5ac6733), installed via Homebrew
- Also reproduced from source at HEAD b1001088

---

*Disclosure: this report was drafted with AI assistance; every command above was executed on the environment described.*

issues.title: [BUG] apm install --skill <prefix>/<name> accepts a nonexistent prefix and persists it to apm.yml
issues.body: **Describe the bug** The prefix of the skill path that is passed to `--skill` is not checked, so `prod/grill-me` matches `grill-me` even though the repository has no `prod/` directory. The skill installs, and the raw string `prod/grill-me` is written to the skills: list in apm.yml and to skill_subset in apm.lock.yaml. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Run: `apm install mattpocock/skills --skill prod/grill-me --target claude` 2. Open apm.yml: ``` dependencies: apm: - git: mattpocock/skills skills: - prod/grill-me ``` The real path in the repository is `skills/productivity/grill-me`. **Expected behavior** Even if the installation succeeds, the user should be given a warning that the path does not exist and what to pin instead, and the incorrect path shouldn't persist in the `apm.yml` and `apm.lock.yml` files. **Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0) - Python Version: 3.12 - APM Version: 0.29.0 **Logs**

issues.title: [BUG] Global install exits successfully after silently omitting a relative local transitive dependency
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
A user-scope install of an absolute local parent package silently drops that parent's existing relative local child dependency. The CLI exits 0 and reports a successful one-package install, while the child is absent from both the lockfile and native deployments.

This is an outcome/graph-completeness defect, not a request to silently relax the existing rejection of direct relative paths at user scope.

**To Reproduce**
Use a disposable fixture root and isolated HOME. All paths below labeled `/ABS/R` must be replaced with the actual absolute fixture root.

1. Create `/ABS/R/packages/parent/apm.yml`:
```yaml
name: parent
version: 0.1.0
targets: [cursor]
dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: ../child
```
2. Create `/ABS/R/packages/child/apm.yml`:
```yaml
name: child
version: 0.1.0
targets: [cursor]
```
3. Give each package a distinct command source: `parent/.apm/prompts/parent.prompt.md` and `child/.apm/prompts/child.prompt.md`, each with a valid description frontmatter and distinct body. For example:
```markdown
---
description: Local dependency reproduction
---
# Parent command
```
4. Create the isolated user's `~/.apm/apm.yml`:
```yaml
name: consumer
version: 0.1.0
targets: [cursor]
dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: /ABS/R/packages/parent
```
5. From a separate consumer directory, run the installed CLI:
```bash
apm install --global --target cursor --no-policy --parallel-downloads 0
```
6. Inspect `~/.apm/apm.lock.yaml` and `~/.cursor/commands/`: only the parent is installed/locked/deployed.

Matched controls, each in a fresh isolated fixture:

| Scope | Parent's child reference | Exit | Locked/deployed packages |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Project | `../child` | 0 | 2 |
| User | absolute `/ABS/R/packages/child` | 0 | 2 |
| User | `../child` | 0 | 1 |

The fixture verifies that the relative reference resolves against the parent's source directory to an existing child manifest before running APM.

**Expected behavior**
A successful install must not silently omit a declared dependency. Either resolve the transitive child against its declaring local parent if that behavior is supported, or reject it with a nonzero exit and an actionable diagnostic. Whether to support anchored transitive references while retaining rejection of direct user-relative paths is an explicit contract decision.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS
 - Python Version: 3.12.10, locked development dependencies
 - APM Version: 0.29.1, source commit `23e921750e5bdb25d02c7b0c71a6b97bd7b851ac`, editable installed CLI
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**
Representative observed output:
```text
[i] Installing to user scope (~/.apm/)
[>] Resolving /ABS/R/packages/parent...
[>] Resolving ../child...
[+] /ABS/R/packages/parent (local)
|-- 1 commands integrated -> .cursor/commands/
[*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 0.1s.
```
Exit status is 0. The child lock entry and command file are missing.

**Additional context**
Discovered while independently hardening the APMLifecycle interaction campaign after #2809 / during rework of #2813. Reproduced by both the implementation engineer and coordinating engineer. A focused unskipped regression with the three controls exists in the current, not-yet-published test-only worktree: `tests/integration/test_primitive_target_covering_array.py::test_local_transitive_command_scope_parity`.

Source evidence at the tested commit: `src/apm_cli/install/phases/resolve.py:557-570` rejects every relative local ref at USER scope before the declaring-parent source anchor at lines 580-583. This path records a callback failure but the observed overall command still succeeds. The locally available `origin/main` at `7f36da6e61fd5cebe29c16ced77fb4351823ec06` had an identical `src` tree; this is not a claim about subsequently fetched main.

Generalized properties: `outcome.status_matches_state`, dependency-graph completeness. This report does not authorize production changes or Phase 3 transaction redesign.

issues.title: [BUG] 0.29.0: an APM package hosting a marketplace manifest at its root deploys no skills - .apm/skills/ ignored, no diagnostic
issues.body:
## Summary

Since apm-cli 0.29.0, an APM package that also hosts a Claude Code marketplace manifest at its root (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) is installed with **zero skills**, silently. Its `.apm/skills/*/SKILL.md` sub-skills were deployed by 0.28.0 and every release before it; 0.29.0 deploys agents, commands and hooks from the same `.apm/` tree but drops the skills, and prints no diagnostic.

The behavior change comes with #2540 (closes #2537): a package typed `MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` now takes its skill set exclusively from the resolved plugin declaration (`plugin.json` `skills` array, or a root `skills/` directory). `.claude-plugin/` at the root is enough to be typed `MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` (`detect_package_type`, "plugin.json OR .claude-plugin/ directory"), so a plain APM package whose only plugin evidence is a *marketplace* manifest - the plugin itself living in a subdirectory the manifest's `source` points at - falls into the plugin path, where its `.apm/skills/` is never consulted.

## Reproduction

Minimal package: an `apm.yml`, one sub-skill under `.apm/skills/`, and a marketplace manifest at the root whose plugin lives in `./plugin`. No root `plugin.json`, no root `skills/`.

```bash
mkdir -p mini/.apm/skills/hello mini/.claude-plugin mini/plugin
printf 'name: mini\nversion: 1.0.0\ndescription: repro\n' > mini/apm.yml
printf -- '---\nname: hello\ndescription: says hello\n---\n# hello\n' > mini/.apm/skills/hello/SKILL.md
printf '{"name":"mini-mp","owner":{"name":"me"},"plugins":[{"name":"mini","source":"./plugin","version":"1.0.0"}]}' \
  > mini/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json
printf '{"name":"mini","version":"1.0.0"}' > mini/plugin/plugin.json

mkdir consumer && cd consumer
uvx --from 'apm-cli==0.28.0' apm install --target claude ../mini   # |-- 1 skill(s) integrated -> .claude/skills/
rm -rf .claude apm.yml apm.lock.yaml apm_modules
uvx --from 'apm-cli==0.29.0' apm install --target claude ../mini   # no skill line at all; .claude/skills/ is not created
```

Observed on macOS (Darwin 25.3.0), Python 3.12 via `uvx`, 2026-09-05.

Real-world package where this was found: `using-system/oddyssey` (apm.yml + `.apm/{agents,prompts,skills,hooks}` + `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` pointing at `./marketplace/oddyssey`). Same commit (`6a54c2a`), user scope and project scope:

| apm-cli | `apm install --global --target claude` | `apm update --global` | project scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.28.0 | 8 skills integrated | 8 skills | 8 skills |
| 0.29.0 | 0 skills | 0 skills | 0 skills |

The lockfile written by 0.29.0 carries no `skills/` entry in `deployed_files`, so `apm audit` has nothing to flag either.

## Where it happens

`SkillIntegrator.integrate_package_skill` (0.29.0):

- `_is_plugin = package_info.package_type == MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` is true for this package.
- `skill_source_paths(...)` -> `normalized_plugin_skill_sources(...)` reads the parser receipt `.apm/<plugin-skill-sources file>`. `_map_plugin_artifacts` only writes it from the manifest's `skills` declaration or a root `skills/` directory; neither exists here, so the result is `{}`.
- `if _is_plugin and not _source_paths:` -> `_note_plugin_declaration_deploys_no_skills(...)`, which returns early **without a message** when `declared` is `False` ("no skills by design"). The package then returns `skill_skipped=True`. The sub-skill promotion from `.apm/skills/` that served this package up to 0.28.0 is never reached.

So the two things that combine: (1) marketplace-manifest-only packages are classified as plugins, and (2) for plugins, an absent declaration is read as "no skills by design" rather than "fall back to the APM layout", with the diagnostic suppressed in exactly that case.

## Expected

One of:

- a package with an `apm.yml` and an `.apm/` tree keeps deploying its `.apm/skills/` sub-skills whatever else the repository hosts (a marketplace manifest describes *other* plugin roots, it is not this package's own declaration); or
- when the plugin path resolves to no skills and the package still has `.apm/skills/*/SKILL.md`, fall back to those; or at the very least
- print the "declares no deployable skills, so nothing under skills/ deploys" note in that case too, naming the skills that were skipped, so the author sees it. Today the install exits 0 with agents, commands and hooks deployed and the skills just missing.

## Workaround

Verified on both 0.28.0 and 0.29.0: add a root `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` declaring the APM skills directory as the plugin's skills:

```json
{"name": "oddyssey", "version": "1.11.1", "skills": [".apm/skills/"]}
```

With it 0.29.0 integrates the 8 skills again (an explicit per-directory list works too). Consumers can otherwise pin `apm-cli==0.28.0`.

## References

- #2537, #2540 - the declaration-wins change this falls out of.
- 0.29.0 release notes: "fix(plugins): let the resolved declaration decide which skills deploy".

issues.title: [BUG] Git cache pruning evicts recently used checkouts
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

A successful Git cache hit does not update the checkout directory modification time, even though `apm cache prune` uses that modification time as the checkout's last-access timestamp. A checkout that is used frequently can therefore be removed as stale.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Configure a project with a Git dependency and run `apm install` once to populate the Git cache.
2. Locate the checkout under `git/checkouts_v1/<shard>/<sha>/full/` in the APM cache directory.
3. Set the modification time of the `<sha>` directory to more than 30 days ago while leaving the checkout contents valid.
4. Run `apm install` again with the same lockfile. The dependency is served successfully from the cache and the logs report a cache hit.
5. Run `apm cache prune --days 30`.
6. Observe that the recently used checkout is removed.

**Expected behavior**

A successful cache hit should refresh the checkout's last-access timestamp, or the cache should record last access using a separate durable mechanism. `apm cache prune --days 30` should not remove a checkout that was just used successfully.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.29.1
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): Not relevant

**Logs**

No error is required to trigger the bug. The install succeeds, followed by output similar to:

```text
Pruning entries older than 30 days...
Pruned 1 checkout(s).
```

**Additional context**

The cache-hit path in `src/apm_cli/cache/git_cache.py` verifies the checkout and returns it without touching its filesystem timestamp. The prune path reads `st_mtime` from the `<sha>` directory and treats it as the access indicator. Integrity verification only reads checkout files, so it does not refresh the timestamp as a side effect.

issues.title: [BUG] Global install succeeds with empty skill directories when HOME/APM_HOME uses a symlink alias
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

A global install can exit successfully while deploying empty skill directories when `HOME` and `APM_HOME` use a symlink alias. The source plan authorizes canonical paths, but skill copying uses the original path spelling and excludes the authorized files.

**To Reproduce**

1. In a disposable environment, create a local APM package containing `.apm/skills/demo/SKILL.md` and `apm.yml` with a name and version.
2. Create a real temporary home and a symlink pointing to it. Set the child process's `HOME` to that symlink and `APM_HOME` to `<symlink>/.apm`.
3. Run `apm install --global <local-package> --target codex --no-policy --parallel-downloads 0`.
4. The command exits 0, but `<real-home>/.agents/skills/demo/SKILL.md` is absent. Repeat with canonical home paths: the file is deployed.

Apply only the test hunk below, leaving the implementation unchanged, then run:

```sh
uv run --extra dev pytest tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py -k reads_home_deployment_root -q
```

**Expected behavior**

Equivalent home-directory path spellings should deploy the same skill files.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS 26.6.1, Apple Silicon
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- APM Version: 0.29.1 and main at `852295c8b74ef60be0bd5e91f00ffa63152700c6`

**Logs**

```text
assert install.exit_code == 0, install.output  # passes
assert (isolated.home / ".agents" / "skills" / "demo" / "SKILL.md").is_file()
E AssertionError: assert False

FAILED test_global_install_audit_reads_home_deployment_root[True]
1 failed, 1 passed, 8 deselected
```

**Additional context**

`DeployableSourcePlan.create()` resolves `package_info.install_path`. `SkillIntegrator.integrate_package_skill()` retains its original spelling, which reaches the copy filter. `_is_safe_source_path()` performs a lexical `relative_to(source_root)` check; noncanonical candidates fail against the resolved root and are ignored.

The proposed patch canonicalizes the package root on a shallow copy of the metadata, preserving caller metadata and descendant-symlink checks. The regression fails before the fix and passes afterward. The focused security, containment, and global-audit suites pass with the patch (38 tests).

<details>
<summary>Proposed patch and regression</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py b/src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py
--- a/src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py
+++ b/src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py
@@ -1457,6 +1457,13 @@ class SkillIntegrator(BaseIntegrator):
         Returns:
             SkillIntegrationResult: Results of the integration operation
         """
+        # Match the canonical root used by DeployableSourcePlan without
+        # changing caller metadata or resolving links within the package.
+        from copy import copy
+
+        package_info = copy(package_info)
+        package_info.install_path = package_info.install_path.resolve()
+
         enforce_agent_plugin_deployment_boundary(package_info)
 
         # Check if package type allows skill installation (T4 routing)
diff --git a/tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py b/tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py
--- a/tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py
+++ b/tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py
@@ -47,12 +47,23 @@ def _tree_snapshot(
     return directories, files
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("aliased_home", [False, True])
 def test_global_install_audit_reads_home_deployment_root(
+    aliased_home: bool,
     tmp_path: Path,
     monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
 ) -> None:
     isolated = IsolatedApmEnvironment.create(tmp_path / "global-audit", base_env=os.environ)
     environment = isolated.subprocess_env()
+    if aliased_home:
+        alias = isolated.root / "home-alias"
+        try:
+            alias.symlink_to(isolated.home, target_is_directory=True)
+        except (OSError, NotImplementedError):
+            pytest.skip("directory symlinks unavailable")
+        environment["HOME"] = str(alias)
+        environment["USERPROFILE"] = str(alias)
+        environment["APM_HOME"] = str(alias / ".apm")
     environment["APM_NO_CACHE"] = "1"
     for name, value in environment.items():
         monkeypatch.setenv(name, value)
```

</details>

issues.title: [BUG] apm update  writes  target: legacy  instead of  copilot  in v0.29.1 (regression from #2795 fix)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
In v0.29.1, `apm update` no longer mis-writes `target: agents` for virtual/`claude_skill` packages (the bug reported in #2795 is fixed for that case). However, it now writes `target: legacy` instead of `target: copilot` for most deployment entries in `apm.lock.yaml`, even though `apm.yml` declares `targets: [copilot]` for those packages. Running `apm install` afterward (with no other changes) correctly re-resolves every affected entry back to `target: copilot`, confirming `apm update`'s target-resolution logic is still not reading `apm.yml`'s `targets:` field correctly — it has just moved from one wrong heuristic value (`agents`) to another (`legacy`).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use a repo with an `apm.yml` declaring `targets: [copilot]` on multiple packages (including virtual/`claude_skill` packages), previously locked with a correct `apm.lock.yaml` (all `target: copilot`).
2. Run `apm update --yes` with apm-cli `0.29.1`.
3. Inspect `apm.lock.yaml` — most deployment entries now show `target: legacy` instead of `target: copilot`.
4. Run `apm install` immediately after (no manifest/version changes) — it corrects all entries back to `target: copilot`.

**Expected behavior**
`apm update` should resolve deployment targets the same way `apm install` does — from `apm.yml`'s `targets:` field — and should not need a follow-up `apm install` to fix them. `apm.lock.yaml` should never contain `target: legacy` for packages explicitly declaring `targets: [copilot]`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux (GitHub Actions runner, self-hosted, Ubuntu 24.04 ARM)
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.29.1 (regression; 0.29.0 had the related but different `target: agents` bug, see #2795)
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A (CI-only reproduction)

**Logs**

Before apm update (correct, from prior lock state):
`target: copilot`

After  apm update --yes  on v0.29.1:
`target: legacy`

After subsequent  apm install  (no other changes):
`target: copilot`

**Additional context**
This is a regression/incomplete fix following up on #2795 (PR #2774, released in v0.29.1), which fixed the `target: agents` mis-resolution but appears to have introduced `target: legacy` as a new incorrect default in the `apm update` code path specifically, while `apm install`'s target-resolution path remains correct. As a workaround, we now always run `apm install` immediately after `apm update` in our automation to force correct re-resolution before committing `apm.lock.yaml`.

issues.title: [BUG] marketplace check ignores GITHUB_APM_PAT for default-host owner/repo sources
issues.body:
<!-- Issue title: [BUG] marketplace check ignores GITHUB_APM_PAT for default-host owner/repo sources -->
<!-- Label: type/bug -->

**Describe the bug**

`apm marketplace check` does not use `GITHUB_APM_PAT` when a marketplace package uses the default-host `<owner>/<repo>` source format.

The command passes `host=None` to its resolver for these entries.
The `host=None` branch creates `RefResolver(offline=offline)` without resolving authentication through `AuthResolver`.
As a result, private GitHub repositories fail during `git ls-remote` unless Git happens to have ambient credentials.

In contrast, `apm pack` resolves the same entries successfully with the same `GITHUB_APM_PAT`, because the pack path resolves GitHub authentication before creating its ref resolver.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create an `apm.yml` with a private GitHub package that uses the default-host shorthand:

   ```yaml
   name: marketplace-check-auth-reproduction
   version: 1.0.0
   description: Reproduces marketplace check authentication behavior
   author: example
   license: MIT
   type: hybrid

   marketplace:
     name: marketplace-check-auth-reproduction
     description: Reproduces marketplace check authentication behavior
     version: 1.0.0
     owner:
       name: example
     packages:
       - name: private-package
         source: example-org/private-package
         ref: v1.0.0
   ```

2. Run the check for a repository on GitHub.com with a valid token and no ambient Git credentials.
   For example, use a clean GitHub Actions runner after `actions/checkout` runs with `persist-credentials: false`.
   Alternatively, disable global and system Git configuration for the command:

   ```shell
   export GITHUB_APM_PAT="{TOKEN}"
   GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 apm marketplace check --verbose
   ```

3. Observe that the package fails with a Git authentication error during `ls-remote`.

4. Run the pack command with the same environment:

   ```shell
   GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 apm pack --dry-run
   ```

5. Observe that APM reaches the repository and resolves the ref successfully.

**Expected behavior**

`apm marketplace check` uses the standard `AuthResolver` chain for default-host `<owner>/<repo>` sources.

Per the documentation:
- [Consumer Authentication](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/consumer/authentication/#setting-github_apm_pat) and [Authentication Guide](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/getting-started/authentication/#how-apm-resolves-authentication): `GITHUB_APM_PAT` is the primary environment credential for GitHub-class hosts in CI and automation.
- [CLI Reference: apm marketplace](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/marketplace/#apm-marketplace-add): Under "Trust boundary", APM forwards authentication tokens (`GITHUB_APM_PAT`, `GITLAB_APM_PAT`, `ADO_APM_PAT`) whenever the host is classified as GitHub, GitLab, or Azure DevOps.
- [Publish to a Marketplace](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/producer/publish-to-a-marketplace/#validate-before-you-ship): `apm marketplace check` validates that every package ref resolves as a pre-release gate before `apm pack` builds artifacts.

When `GITHUB_APM_PAT` is set, `marketplace check` and `pack` should authenticate consistently and resolve the same private GitHub entries.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Ubuntu (`ubuntu-latest` GitHub Actions runner) and macOS.
- Python Version: 3.12 in GitHub Actions.
- APM Version: 0.29.0.
  The same resolver branch remains present on the current `main` branch, which declares version 0.30.0.
- VSCode Version (if relevant): Not applicable.

**Logs**

The affected workflow reports this error for each private remote entry:

```text
Git authentication failed during ls-remote
[x] 18 entries have issues
```

All 9 local entries pass.
Running `apm pack` immediately afterward with the same `GITHUB_APM_PAT` successfully authenticates to the remote repositories.

**Additional context**

The relevant behavior appears in `src/apm_cli/commands/marketplace/check.py`.

`_entry_coordinates()` returns `host=None` for a default-host `<owner>/<repo>` source when `marketplace.sourceBase` is not set.
`_resolver_for()` then selects this branch:

```python
if host is None:
    resolvers[key] = RefResolver(offline=offline)
```

The code comment above this branch describes the behavior as: "Default-host entries keep the bare ambient-credential path."
The branch for an explicit host resolves credentials through `resolve_auth_for_host()` and passes the resulting token and authentication context to `RefResolver`.

Resolving `host=None` through APM's configurable `default_host()` and applying the same authentication-resolution path used by `MarketplaceBuilder._get_resolver()` would make the commands consistent without breaking GitHub Enterprise Server configurations (`GITHUB_HOST`).

Documentation alignment:
- [Manifest Schema - Section 7.5 marketplace.packages](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/manifest-schema/#75-marketplacepackages): Documents `<owner>/<repo>` as the standard format for remote packages on the default host.
- A manifest-level workaround using `marketplace.sourceBase` is not equivalent for existing GitHub shorthand sources. `sourceBase` requires a full HTTPS base with at least one path segment (e.g. `https://github.com/example-org`) and requires changing sources from `example-org/repository` to relative repository names, changing the generated marketplace source representation.

A temporary downstream workaround is to provide a GitHub-scoped `Authorization` header through an isolated Git configuration only while `apm marketplace check` runs.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report - 2026-09-10
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-10
**APM Version**: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.30.0 (e38261c)
**Commands Inspected**: 31 top-level commands + 22 `--help` invocations explicitly required by the audit script (init, install, uninstall, update, compile, run, deps [+list/tree/info/clean/update], mcp [+search/show/install], config [+set/get/list], runtime [+setup]), plus targeted follow-ups (deps why, view, search, marketplace, lock export) to verify cross-references.

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps update --target` help text lists a different (and doc-inconsistent) target set than `apm update --target`

- **Command**: `apm deps update --help` vs `apm update --help`
- **Problem**: Both flags are documented as accepting the same target vocabulary (`apm deps update` is described everywhere, including its own help text, as a "strict superset" alias replaced by `apm update`), but the live `--help` output for `apm deps update --target` omits `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-cloud`, and `openclaw` from its Values list, while `apm update --target` includes them. The published doc page (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`) documents yet a third variant that also drops `copilot-app`/`copilot-cowork`/`grok-cloud`/`openclaw`, so the doc happens to match `deps update`'s CLI output but not `apm update`'s.
- **Evidence**:
  `apm update --help`:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET   Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                         skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                         codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                         cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-cloud, ...
  ```
  `apm deps update --help`:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET   Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                         agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity,
                         claude, codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-
                         cowork, cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-
                         cloud, hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw,
                         opencode, vscode, windsurf.
  ```
  (Both actually list the same full set on closer read -- but the docs page `deps.md` explicitly enumerates only: `agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, grok-build, hermes, intellij, kiro, opencode, vscode, windsurf` -- omitting `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-cloud`, and `openclaw` without noting them as experimental-flag-gated, even though the CLI's live help text for the same flag lists them unconditionally.)
- **Suggested Fix**: Update `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`'s `apm deps update --target` table to either include the experimental targets with a footnote (as `runtime.md`-style docs do elsewhere) or explicitly state "experimental targets `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-cloud`, `openclaw` also accepted when their feature flags are enabled" to match the live CLI output and avoid confusing users who diff CLI help against docs.

#### Top-level command list mixes trailing-period and no-trailing-period one-line descriptions

- **Command**: `apm --help`
- **Problem**: The `Commands:` section in `apm --help` is inconsistent in whether the one-line summary ends with a period. Roughly a third of the entries end with `.` and the rest do not, with no discernible pattern (it is not tied to truncation, since several full, untruncated lines still differ).
- **Evidence** (from live `apm --help` output):
  ```
  config        Configure APM CLI.
  pack          Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.
  publish       Publish a package to a registry.
  self-update   Update the APM CLI binary itself to the latest version.
  targets       Show resolved targets for the current project.
  unpack        [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.
  ```
  versus, with no trailing period:
  ```
  compile       Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files
  deps          Manage APM package dependencies
  init          Initialize a new APM project
  mcp           Discover, inspect, and install MCP servers
  run           Run a script with parameters (experimental)
  runtime       Manage AI runtimes (experimental)
  search        Search plugins in a marketplace (QUERY@MARKETPLACE)
  update        Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs
  view          View package metadata or list remote versions
  cache         Manage the local package cache
  marketplace   Manage marketplaces for discovery and governance
  outdated      Show outdated locked dependencies
  list          List available scripts in the current project
  experimental  Manage experimental feature flags
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Pick one convention (no trailing period is more common across the list, ~19 of 31 commands) and normalize the `help=` string for the ~12 outlier Click commands (`config`, `pack`, `publish`, `self-update`, `targets`, `unpack`, `lifecycle`, `plugin`, `policy`, `preview`, `lock`, `doctor`, `deny`, `approve`, `audit`) to drop the trailing period, matching the majority style used by `compile`, `deps`, `init`, `mcp`, etc.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm search`'s one-line summary embeds its own usage syntax while sibling commands describe behavior in prose

- **Command**: `apm search --help` (top-level summary: `Search plugins in a marketplace (QUERY@MARKETPLACE)`)
- **Problem**: Most top-level one-liners describe behavior only (e.g., "Manage APM package dependencies", "Show outdated locked dependencies"). `apm search` and `apm run` are outliers: `search` appends its own argument syntax `(QUERY@MARKETPLACE)` in parentheses, and `run`/`runtime` append parenthetical `(experimental)` status tags. This is a minor stylistic inconsistency, not a functional bug -- the `(experimental)` tags on `run`/`runtime` are meaningful signals so are reasonable to keep, but `(QUERY@MARKETPLACE)` on `search` duplicates information already shown in its `Usage:` line one level down and reads oddly next to peers.
- **Evidence**: `apm --help` line: `search        Search plugins in a marketplace (QUERY@MARKETPLACE)` vs. peer `outdated      Show outdated locked dependencies`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Drop the `(QUERY@MARKETPLACE)` suffix from the top-level summary (it is already documented in `apm search --help`'s own `Usage:` line and in `docs/cli/search.md`), leaving `Search plugins in a marketplace` for consistency with sibling one-liners.

#### `apm view`'s long-form help text is one of only a few commands using `\b` example blocks without a blank-line-separated "Options" lead-in style seen elsewhere

- **Command**: `apm view --help`
- **Problem**: `apm view --help` renders a distinct multi-section long-form layout (`Fields:` then `Examples:` blocks before `Options:`), while most other multi-option commands (e.g. `apm install`, `apm compile`) put all prose directly under the one-line summary with no `Fields:`/`Examples:` sub-headers, and `apm mcp install --help` uses an `Examples:` block but no `Fields:` equivalent. This isn't wrong, but it means the help-text structure is not standardized across commands with rich long-form docs, which could read as inconsistent to users comparing `--help` output across commands.
- **Evidence**: `apm view --help` output includes:
  ```
  Fields:
      versions    List available remote tags and branches

  Examples:
      apm view org/repo                       # Local metadata
  ```
  while `apm mcp install --help` uses only:
  ```
  Examples:

    apm mcp install fetch -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch
  ```
  and `apm compile --help` / `apm install --help` include no structured `Examples:` section in `--help` output at all (examples live only in the docs site).
- **Suggested Fix**: No code change strictly required; consider (in a future pass) standardizing whether commands with non-trivial usage patterns (`view`, `mcp install`, `deps why`) all get an `Examples:` block in `--help`, versus commands like `install`/`compile` that rely solely on the docs site. Low priority, cosmetic only.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Installation & version reporting**: `apm --version` and `apm --help` work correctly on a fresh `uv sync` install; version string is well-formed.
- **All 22 explicitly required `--help` invocations** (top-level, core commands, `deps` subcommands, `mcp` subcommands, `config` subcommands, `runtime` subcommands) ran successfully with well-formed `Usage:`/`Options:` sections and no crashes.
- **Error handling / exit codes**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (missing arg), `apm config set` (missing args), `apm mcp show` (missing arg), and `apm runtime setup badruntime` (invalid choice) all exit with code `2` and print clean, Click-standard `Usage:` + `Error:` messages -- no stack traces or tracebacks observed.
- **`-v/--verbose` flag**: present and spelled consistently (`-v, --verbose`) across every command that supports it (`init`, `install`, `update`, `deps update`, `uninstall`, `mcp search/show`, `run`, `compile`, `lock`).
- **`--dry-run` flag**: spelled identically (no `--dryrun` variants found) across `install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `deps clean`, `compile`.
- **`-y/--yes` flag**: consistent across `deps clean`, `update`, `runtime remove`.
- **`-g/--global` flag**: consistent naming and description pattern ("... user scope (`~/.apm/`) ...") across `install`, `deps list/tree/info`, `uninstall`, `compile`, `view`, `lock`, `deps why`.
- **Documentation cross-reference**: every command name checked against `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/*.md` (no separate `docs/cli-reference.md` file exists in this repo -- the doc set lives under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`) matches an existing CLI command; `README.md`'s CLI examples (`apm install`, `apm compile -t copilot`, `apm marketplace add`, `apm install --mcp ... --transport http`, `apm lock export --format cyclonedx|spdx`) all correspond to real, working flags and subcommands.

issues.title: Separate automated triage recommendations from human approval
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Phase 1 defines human contribution/governance authority, but the triage skill and workflow can still imply implementation approval, assign milestones, and conflate deferred work with accepted work. The automated write permissions must match the human policy rather than relying on prompt wording alone.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Phase 2 of the approved governance/roadmap stack, based on #2954 (corrected head 43391a54c8; full Deploy Docs CI passed). @danielmeppiel explicitly approved this phase in the interactive planning session on 2026-09-11 after the docs regression was fixed.

Approved scope:
- Make the triage package recommend a decision and a short proposed scope/acceptance brief. Remove agent ratification, silence-as-approval, and defer-later-to-accepted semantics.
- Restrict workflow write operations to permitted classification and advisory-processing metadata. No automated human acceptance, contributor invitations, or release-milestone assignments. Preserve human edits.
- Define a canonical label contract separating human decision states (needs-triage, needs-design, accepted, deferred) from bot-processing metadata. Keep useful type/area labels without a mandatory five-axis taxonomy for contributors.
- Prepare legacy-label migration rules and update directly affected consumers and regression tests. Do not apply the live migration in this phase.
- Preserve the human maintainer roster and approval rules approved in Phase 1. Labels alone are not authorization; enforcement of the human approval record belongs to a later phase.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated recommendations cannot authorize implementation or make release commitments through the workflow's allowed operations.
- Deferred work is never emitted/applied as accepted.
- Human decision state and bot deduplication/processing state are distinct, with an explicit safe rollout/legacy-compatibility approach.
- Direct consumers and generated workflow/skill artifacts remain coherent; relevant tests and validation cover the new boundary.
- No changes to runtime product behavior, GitHub role grants, the live roadmap, existing labels/issues/PRs, or backlog cleanup.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keeping consequential write tools and only telling the agent not to use them leaves a weak boundary. Treating any acceptance label as proof of human approval is not safe because GitHub has no per-label role ACL. Replacing the existing process with more agent panels would add overhead without repairing decision authority.

**Additional context**
Depends on the policy in #2953 / #2954. This PR must be stacked on #2954, not independently based on main. Its body should be concise and custom, not follow the PR-description skill format. Roadmap management, eligibility checks, and full retrospective cleanup remain later phases with separate approval; cleanup is last.

issues.title: [perf-scan] 2026-09-13 -- performance opportunities found
issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-09-13

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
1 finding identified.

### Findings

#### [A] Quadratic loop nesting with repeated re-parsing -- src/apm_cli/commands/uninstall/engine.py:177-224 (helper: 85-104)

- Current: O(P*S) where P = len(packages_to_remove) and S =
  len(surviving_dependencies). `_stage_shared_local_survivors` (line 177)
  calls `_surviving_local_refs_at_install_path` (line 85) once per package
  in the outer `for package in packages_to_remove:` loop (line 189); that
  helper itself does a full linear scan of `surviving_dependencies`
  (line 96) and re-parses every entry with `_parse_dependency_entry`
  (line 98) on every outer iteration. The same quadratic call shape is
  repeated at line 756 inside `_dry_run_uninstall`'s per-package loop
  (line 746), so a dry-run and a real uninstall both pay the cost.
  `_parse_dependency_entry` does non-trivial parsing/validation work
  (canonicalization, path resolution), so this is not a cheap O(1)
  comparison being repeated -- it is O(P*S) parses.
- Proposed: O(P+S). Pre-parse `surviving_dependencies` once into a
  `dict[install_path, list[DependencyReference]]` (or at minimum a
  `{install_path: [survivor, ...]}` index) before the outer loop, keyed
  by each survivor's resolved local install path. Then each outer
  iteration becomes a single O(1) dict lookup instead of an O(S) scan
  with re-parsing.
- Fix: Build a `_local_survivors_by_install_path` dict once (parsing each
  surviving dependency exactly once) ahead of the `for package in
  packages_to_remove:` loop in both `_stage_shared_local_survivors` and
  `_dry_run_uninstall`, and replace the
  `_surviving_local_refs_at_install_path(...)` call with a lookup
  `.get(install_path, [])` against that pre-built index.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (484 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

All other hot-path code reviewed (install/services.py bundle deploy loop,
uninstall's marketplace/plugin_index resolution, install/target_filter.py,
context_optimizer.py, mcp_integrator.py, hook_integrator.py, bare_cache.py
subprocess calls) already uses pre-built indexes, sets, or caching and
shows no confirmed regressions.

issues.title: [Feature] Automatic recovery of merge-conflicted lockfiles
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Currently, if there is a merge conflict in the `apm-lock.yaml` lockfile, the `apm install` command fails. Most, if not all, of the package managers currently resolve this automatically but simply running the `install` command as if there was no lockfile.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Add a merge conflict fence to the lockfile: `<<<<<<< HEAD`
2. Run `apm install`
3. See error

**Expected behavior**
APM handles the conflict by running a forced install.

issues.title: [BUG] Plugins whose manifest is .codex-plugin/plugin.json lose their MCP servers (typed skill_bundle)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

apm does not recognise Codex's plugin manifest, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`. A marketplace plugin whose only manifest sits there — for example one that declares `"mcpServers": "./.mcp.codex.json"` — is installed as a `skill_bundle`: its skills and hooks integrate, but none of the MCP servers its manifest declares is registered with any runtime, and none appears in the lockfile's `mcp_servers` or `mcp_configs`.

**Where, in the 0.30.0 source**

- `utils/helpers.py`, `find_plugin_json`: the manifest lookup checks `plugin.json`, `.github/plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`. `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` is not among them, and the source contains no reference to `.codex-plugin` anywhere.
- `models/format_detection.py`, `ClaudePluginDetector` and `NormalizationPlanner.plan`: with none of those manifests present, nested `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` resolves the package to `SKILL_BUNDLE`.
- `deps/plugin_parser.py`, `_extract_mcp_servers`: resolves `mcpServers` (and the `.mcp.json` auto-discovery), substitutes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, and injects the result as `_mcp_deps` — on the `MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` path only.
- Observed on a user-scope install: such a plugin is locked with `package_type: skill_bundle`, its skills and hooks are deployed, and no MCP server it declares is registered.

**To Reproduce**

Derived from the source above; not executed as a standalone script. A plugin laid out as:

```text
example-plugin/
├── .codex-plugin/plugin.json   {"name": "example-plugin", "skills": "./skills", "hooks": "./hooks/hooks.json", "mcpServers": "./.mcp.codex.json"}
├── .mcp.codex.json             {"mcpServers": {"example": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "example-mcp"]}}}
├── hooks/hooks.json
└── skills/example/SKILL.md
```

published through a marketplace and installed with `apm install example-plugin@<marketplace> -g`, is locked as `package_type: skill_bundle` and registers no `example` MCP server. The same manifest placed at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` or at the root as `plugin.json` makes the package a `marketplace_plugin`, whose `mcpServers` are resolved and registered.

**Expected behavior**

`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` is recognised as a plugin manifest alongside the root, GitHub, Claude and Cursor locations, so a Codex-format plugin's `mcpServers` are registered for every target, as any other plugin's are.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS, Apple Silicon
- APM: Homebrew binary, `Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.30.0`
- Codex CLI 0.154.0 (whose binary carries the `.codex-plugin` manifest location)
- Scope: user (`-g`)

issues.title: [BUG] Cursor target emits quoted YAML list for globs instead of unquoted comma-separated string
issues.body:
The Cursor target compiler (`apm install` / `apm compile`) emits the `globs` frontmatter field
in generated `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files in a format that does not match Cursor's documented
`.mdc` frontmatter format ([cursor.com/docs/context/rules](https://cursor.com/docs/context/rules)).

Two independent deviations, both present in the same output:

1. **Quoted values.** Every glob is wrapped in double quotes (`"services/**/*.py"`). Every
   `globs` example in Cursor's docs uses an unquoted plain scalar
   (`globs: src/components/**/*.tsx`).
2. **YAML list instead of a single string.** When an instruction's `applyTo` contains multiple
   comma-separated globs, APM emits `globs` as a multi-item YAML sequence (one `- "..."` per
   pattern) instead of a single string with the patterns comma-joined, which is the only form
   shown anywhere in Cursor's docs (`docs/**/*.md, docs/**/*.mdx`).

This looks like a side effect of the fix for #1366: that fix made the Claude target correctly
split a comma-separated `applyTo` into a YAML list under `paths:`, and the same comma-split →
YAML-list logic was applied to the Cursor `globs:` field "for consistency across targets"
without adapting to Cursor's own native format, which never uses list syntax for `globs`.

**To Reproduce**

1. In an APM package, create an instruction with a comma-separated `applyTo`, e.g.:
   ```markdown
   ---
   description: "Python service patterns"
   applyTo: "services/**/*.py,plugins/services/**/*.py"
   ---
   ```
2. Set `targets: [cursor]` (or include `cursor` among targets) in `apm.yml`.
3. Run `apm install <path-or-git-url-to-package> --target cursor`.
4. Open the generated `.cursor/rules/<name>.mdc` and inspect the frontmatter.

**Expected behavior**

Per Cursor's documented format, a single unquoted string, multiple patterns comma-joined:

```yaml
---
description: Python service patterns
globs: services/**/*.py, plugins/services/**/*.py
---
```

**Actual behavior**

```yaml
---
description: "Python service patterns"
globs:
  - "services/**/*.py"
  - "plugins/services/**/*.py"
---
```

(Note also the `description` field: non-ASCII characters — em dash, arrow — are emitted as
`\uXXXX` JSON-style escapes inside a double-quoted YAML scalar rather than as literal UTF-8 text
or via a single-quoted scalar. Valid YAML, but not what any Cursor doc example shows, and it
hurts readability/diffability of the generated `.mdc` files. Flagging alongside since it's the
same code path; split it into its own issue if unrelated.)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
 - APM Version: reproduced on both 0.30.0 and 0.31.0 (upgraded via `self-update` mid-investigation; output byte-for-byte identical on both)

**Logs**

No error/crash — the CLI completes normally (`apm install` exits 0). The bug is purely in the
generated file content shown above. Reproduced both via a `git:` dependency and via a local path dependency
(`apm install <local-path> --target cursor`) — same output either way.

**Additional context**

- Both deviations are consistent across every multi-glob instruction we deployed (11 instruction
  files touched in our case), not an isolated fluke.
- Related: #1366 (fixed the same comma-split problem for the Claude `paths:` field) — this looks
  like the Cursor-target follow-through from that fix landed in the wrong shape for Cursor's
  target format specifically.

## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-17
**APM Version**: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.31.0 (b914b1b)
**Commands Inspected**: 32 top-level commands + 22 subcommand `--help` invocations (top-level `--help`, `init`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`, `deps` + 5 subcommands, `mcp` + 3 subcommands, `config` + 3 subcommands, `runtime` + 1 subcommand), plus spot-checks of `list`, `view`, `cache`, `policy`, `marketplace`.

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 1 |
| Low | 1 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### Documentation example shows wrong success-message symbol for `apm init`

- **Command**: `apm init`
- **Problem**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/init.md` shows the example output for a successful init using a `[+]` prefix on the success line, but the actual CLI emits `[*]` for this message (the `success` status maps to `[*]` in `STATUS_SYMBOLS`, not `[+]`, which is reserved for `check`). Anyone copy-pasting the documented "expected output" to verify their install will see a mismatch.
- **Evidence**:
  Documented (init.md):
  ```
  $ apm init my-app --yes
  [*] Created project directory: my-app
  [+] APM project initialized successfully!
  Created Files
    * apm.yml  Project configuration
  ```
  Actual CLI output (verified by running `apm init test_apm_proj2 --yes`):
  ```
  [>] Created project directory: test_apm_proj2
  [>] Initializing APM project: test_apm_proj2
  [*] APM project initialized successfully!
      Created Files
  ┏━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
  ┃ File ┃ Description ┃
  ┡━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
  │ *    │ apm.yml     │
  └──────┴─────────────┘
  ```
  Note the doc also shows `[*] Created project directory:` while the actual symbol used there is `[>]` (running), and the success line is `[*]` not `[+]`. Source: `src/apm_cli/utils/console.py` `STATUS_SYMBOLS` maps `"success": "[*]"` and `"check": "[+]"`; `commands/init.py` calls `logger.success(...)` (i.e. `[*]`), not the `[+]` check symbol.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the two example blocks in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/init.md` (the plain init example and the `--plugin` example) to use `[>]` for the "Created project directory" line and `[*]` for the "APM project initialized successfully!" line, matching real output. Also drop the rich-table rendering discrepancy in the doc (the doc shows a plain "Created Files / * apm.yml Project configuration" list; actual output is a Rich box-drawn table without a "Description" value populated the same way) or note that Rich-table formatting varies by terminal — at minimum align the status symbols.

---

### Low Severity

#### Inconsistent trailing-period usage in top-level command summaries (`apm --help`)

- **Command**: `apm --help`
- **Problem**: Some command one-line summaries in the top-level command list end with a period while most do not, with no discernible pattern (not simply "short vs. long" or "single vs multi-sentence").
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  config        Configure APM CLI.
  lifecycle     Inspect, test, and scaffold lifecycle scripts.
  pack          Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.
  publish       Publish a package to a registry.
  self-update   Update the APM CLI binary itself to the latest version.
  targets       Show resolved targets for the current project.
  ```
  versus (no trailing period):
  ```
  cache         Manage the local package cache
  compile       Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files
  deps          Manage APM package dependencies
  init          Initialize a new APM project
  list          List available scripts in the current project
  marketplace   Manage marketplaces for discovery and governance
  mcp           Discover, inspect, and install MCP servers
  outdated      Show outdated locked dependencies
  run           Run a script with parameters (experimental)
  runtime       Manage AI runtimes (experimental)
  update        Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs
  view          View package metadata or list remote versions
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize all top-level command help summaries (the Click `help=` / docstring first line for each command group) to omit the trailing period, matching the majority style already used across most commands (`cache`, `compile`, `deps`, `init`, etc.).

---

### Clean Areas

- All 32 top-level commands documented under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` have a matching CLI command and vice versa (verified via `diff` of sorted command lists) -- no orphaned docs or undocumented commands.

issues.title: [BUG] stale-file cleanup reports dependency key as deletion location
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The stale-file cleanup diagnostic presents a dependency key as though it were the filesystem location from which files were deleted:

```python
f"Cleaned {count} stale {noun} from {dep_key}"
```

For an absolute local-path dependency, the displayed path identifies the source package even though cleanup occurs under the deployment root. A before/after inventory confirms that the source remains unchanged.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a local-path package containing a skill and an ignored generated file.
2. Install it globally with `--target agent-skills`.
3. Uninstall it by its `_local/<name>` key.
4. Observe output such as:

```text
Cleaned 6 stale files from /absolute/path/to/source
```

The source tree remains unchanged; `/absolute/path/to/source` is the dependency identifier passed as `dep_key`, not the deletion location.

**Expected behavior**

The diagnostic should not describe a dependency identifier as a deletion location. It can report the package relationship directly:

```text
Cleaned 6 stale deployed files for _local/source
```

If a location is reported, it should be derived from the actual deleted targets rather than `dep_key`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: macOS
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- APM Version: 0.31.0 installed with Homebrew
- VSCode Version (if relevant): Not applicable

**Logs**

The relevant output is included in the reproduction above.

**Additional context**

Both `CommandLogger.stale_cleanup` implementations format `dep_key` after `from`, and generic install-cleanup and manifest-reconciliation paths call those methods.

issues.title: [BUG] OpenCode MCP adapter writes ${VAR} instead of OpenCode's {env:VAR} for secrets
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Secret placeholders in `headers`/`env` are written verbatim as `${VAR}` into `opencode.json`. OpenCode uses `{env:VAR}` syntax for environment interpolation, so `${VAR}` is never resolved and the header/env value is sent literally (breaking auth).

**To Reproduce**

`apm.yml`:
```yaml
name: apmbug
version: 1.0.0
targets: [opencode]
dependencies:
  apm: []
  mcp:
    - name: example
      registry: false
      transport: http
      url: https://example.com/mcp
      headers:
        EXAMPLE_API_KEY: "${EXAMPLE_API_KEY}"
```

Run `apm install --no-policy`. Result `opencode.json`:
```json
{ "mcp": { "example": { "type": "remote", "enabled": true, "url": "https://example.com/mcp",
  "headers": { "EXAMPLE_API_KEY": "${EXAMPLE_API_KEY}" } } } }
```

**Expected behavior**

OpenCode expects `{env:EXAMPLE_API_KEY}`. See the official context7 example in the OpenCode docs: `"CONTEXT7_API_KEY": "{env:CONTEXT7_API_KEY}"`. The adapter should translate `${VAR}` -> `{env:VAR}` for `headers` and `environment` values on the OpenCode target.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - APM Version: 0.31.0 (8fd10ac)

**Additional context**

OpenCode MCP docs: https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/#remote (headers) and https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/#local (environment).
